Eventually, a passing whale saw what was happening and came to help the turtles. He used his big tail to knock the penguin off the box. The big penguin was so sad and ran away. The whale freed the turtles and they ran back to the sea, safe and sound. 

But the big penguin was so upset he thought he would never be able to play again. He was so sad that he went away and never came back.

Then the bear took a piece of wood and measured the dry bed. When he was done, he said, "The bed is very big, but it is not very deep!" Everyone smiled and the bear thought of a clever idea. He said, "Let us fill the river bed with jam. It will be like a big, sweet river!"

The animals all cheered and immediately started filling up the river bed with jam. Soon the dry bed was filled with a delicious, sweet river of jam. Everyone had so much fun that they decided to do it again every day!

"I'm looking for carrots," replied the bunny.

Just then, a lightning bolt struck a nearby tree. The bunny was scared and ran away. The man watched as the bunny hopped away into the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her rubber duck in the bathtub every night before bed. One day, Lily's mom told her not to splash too much water on the floor or she would be punished.

Lily didn't listen and splashed water all over the floor. Her mom saw it and said, "Lily, you didn't listen to me. You will be punished."

Lily was fearful and didn't know what would happen. The next day, when she went to play with her rubber duck, it was gone. Her mom had taken it away as punishment for not listening.

Lily learned her lesson and promised to listen to her mom from then on. She never wanted to lose her rubber duck again.

Lily went outside to show her friend, Timmy. "Look, Timmy! I'm a princess with magic powers!" she said. But Timmy didn't believe her. "That's silly, Lily. There's no such thing as magic."

Lily was sad that Timmy didn't believe her. She wanted to quit playing with him. But then she remembered something her mom told her: "If you believe in yourself, anything is possible." So, she closed her eyes and imagined herself casting a magic spell.

When she opened her eyes, Timmy was amazed. "Wow, Lily! You really do have magic powers!" he said. Lily was happy that she didn't quit and that she proved Timmy wrong. From then on, they played together and had lots of fun using their magic powers.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. Tweety knew that when there was a big, dark cloud, there might be lightning.

Tweety flew faster to get to her nest before the lightning came. But Tweety forgot where her nest was! She searched and searched but couldn't find it. Just then, she saw a big tree with a hole in it. Tweety thought it might be useful to hide in the hole until the lightning went away.

As Tweety flew into the hole, she noticed that it was a little bit of a struggle to fit inside. But she kept trying and finally, she made it in. Just as she settled in, she heard a loud BOOM! The lightning had come, but Tweety was safe in her little hole. From then on, Tweety always remembered where her nest was and never forgot how useful a safe place can be.

The lion learned that even though they spoke different languages, they could still be friends and have a peaceful time together.

Her mommy explained to her, "Lily, sometimes we have to wait for things to be ready before we can share them. Just like how we wait for cookies to bake in the oven before we can eat them. Your picture will be even more special when it's dry and ready to be sent to the museum."

Lily understood and waited patiently for her picture to dry. When it was ready, her mommy sent it to the museum. Everyone who saw it loved it, and Lily felt very proud. She learned that sometimes we have to be patient and wait for things to be ready before we can share them with others.

One day, a little fish was swimming by. The shark saw the little fish and wanted to eat it. But the little fish was too fast and swam away. The shark was sad.

Then, the little fish had an idea. It swam to a big piece of seaweed and started to wrap it around itself. The shark swam by and saw the little fish wrapped up in the seaweed. The shark thought it was just seaweed and swam away.

The little fish was happy it tricked the shark and swam away safely. And the shark continued to swim around the beautiful ocean, looking for something else to eat. The end.

Sara loved to make things with her mom. They had a big box of cloth and thread and needles. Sara learned how to make a stitch with her mom's help. She wanted to make a gift for her dad.

One day, Sara found a blue cloth with stars on it. She thought it was perfect for her dad. He liked to look at the stars at night. Sara asked her mom if she could use it. Her mom said yes, but she had to be careful with the needle. It was sharp and could hurt her.

Sara was enthusiastic. She cut a big square of the cloth and folded it in half. She used a pencil to draw a heart on it. She wanted to stitch the heart with red thread. She asked her mom to help her start. Her mom made a knot at the end of the thread and showed Sara how to push the needle through the cloth.

Sara followed her mom's instructions. She made small stitches along the pencil line. She was proud of her work. She trusted her mom to teach her well. She smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

Her mom smiled back and said, "I love you too, Sara. You're doing great. Keep going. Your dad will love your gift."

Sara finished the heart and tied a knot. She cut the thread and opened the cloth. She saw the heart on both sides. She was happy. She hugged her mom and said, "Look, mom. I made a heart for dad. Do you think he will like it?"

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I think he will love it, Sara. You made it with love and care. You are a wonderful daughter. Let's go and give it to him. He's waiting for us."

Sara and her mom went to find her dad. He was in the living room, reading a book. He looked up and saw them. He smiled and said, "Hello, my girls. What do you have there?"

Sara ran to him and said, "Dad, dad, I made you a gift. Look, it's a star cloth with a heart. I stitched it myself. Mom helped me. Do you like it?"

Her dad was surprised and touched. He took the cloth and looked at it. He saw the stars and the heart and the stitches. He felt the love and the care. He said, "Sara, this is the most beautiful gift I ever got. I love it. I love you. You are a wonderful daughter. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

He hugged Sara and kissed her. He hugged her mom and kissed her. They all smiled and laughed. They were a happy family. Sara felt warm and cozy. She was glad she made the gift. She was glad she trusted her mom. She was glad she loved her dad. She was glad they loved her. She thought, "This is the best day ever."

Sam said, "Be careful, Tim. We don't know if it's good to eat." Tim tasted the red plant anyway. It was very yummy. Tim and Sam were happy they found a new part of the swamp and a new yummy plant to eat. They went home and told their friends about their adventure.

The bee was very happy. It flew to the big red flower and got food. Then, the bee thanked Mia for her help. Mia and the bee became good friends, and they played in the garden every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved jam. She loved jam so much that she would eat it every day. One day, Sue's mom said, "Sue, we have no more jam. We need to go to the store to buy some more."

At the store, Sue saw a big jar of dark red jam. She wanted it so much. But there were only a few jars left. Sue saw another little boy who also wanted the dark red jam. The little boy said, "I want that jam too!"

Sue thought that they should number the jars to see who would get the last one. She said, "Let's count the jars. One, two, three... There are three jars. We can each have one and leave one for someone else." The little boy agreed, and they each took a jar of the dark red jam.

Sue was happy that she could have her favorite jam again. She learned that sharing is important and that sometimes, counting can help solve problems. And from that day on, Sue and the little boy became good friends, sharing their love for the dark red jam.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play in the woods. She had a red coat and a basket of food for her grandma. She knew the way to grandma's house very well. She did not need to ask anyone for help.

One day, she met a big wolf in the woods. The wolf had sharp teeth and a long tail. He was hungry and wanted to eat Lily. He said, "Hello, little girl. Where are you going?"

Lily was not afraid of the wolf. She said, "I am going to grandma's house. She is sick and needs some food. Do you want to come with me?"

The wolf was surprised by Lily's answer. He thought she would run away or scream. He said, "Yes, I would like to come with you. But can I ask you something? Why are you not scared of me? Don't you know I am a wolf?"

Lily said, "Yes, I know you are a wolf. But I also know you are a humble wolf. You do not lie or hurt others. You only eat when you are hungry. You are not like the bad wolves who are mean and greedy. You are a good wolf, and I am your friend."

The wolf was touched by Lily's words. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very kind and brave. You are a good friend, too. I will not eat you or your grandma. I will share your food and keep you safe."

So Lily and the wolf walked together to grandma's house. They had a nice picnic with grandma, who was happy to see them. They told stories and laughed and played. Lily and the wolf became the best of friends. They learned from each other and helped each other. They were happy and humble in the woods.

Tom loves to zoom his toy rocket. He makes it fly in the air and makes loud noises. He pretends he is an astronaut and goes to space. He likes to see the stars and the moon and the planets.

One day, he zooms his rocket too high. It goes out of the window and into the sky. Tom is sad and scared. He thinks he lost his rocket forever. He cries and runs to his mom.

Mom hugs Tom and tells him not to worry. She says she has a surprise for him. She takes him to the backyard and shows him a big telescope. She says they can look at space together and maybe find his rocket.

Tom is happy and curious. He looks through the telescope and sees many things. He sees the sun and the clouds and the birds. He sees a plane and a balloon and a kite. He sees a shiny dot that moves fast. He thinks it is his rocket.

Mom says it is a satellite. She says it is a machine that helps people talk and watch TV. She says it is noisy because it has a big engine. She says it is like his rocket, but bigger and smarter.

Tom thinks that is cool. He says he wants to be a satellite when he grows up. He says he wants to zoom in space and help people. He says he loves his mom and his rocket and his telescope. He says he loves space.

Lisa wanted to give her mom a beautiful gift for her birthday. She found a black scarf in her mom's closet that she never wore. Lisa thought it was very soft and shiny. She decided to wrap it with some paper and a bow that she found in a drawer.

She was very happy with her gift and ran to the living room to hide it behind the couch. She waited for her mom to come home from work. She wanted to surprise her and make her smile.

But when her mom came home, she looked very sad and tired. She saw the black scarf on the couch and picked it up. She said, "Oh no, this is my grandma's scarf. She gave it to me before she died. It is very special to me. How did it get here?"

Lisa came out from behind the couch and said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I wanted to give you a beautiful gift. I thought you didn't like the scarf. I wrapped it for you. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Lisa, you are very sweet and thoughtful. I'm not mad at you. I'm sorry I was sad. I miss my grandma very much. She loved you too. You know what? She would want you to have the scarf. It is beautiful, just like you. You can wear it and remember her. Thank you for your gift. I love you."

Sam and Tom were friends who liked to run. They ran every day in the park. They wanted to win a medal in the big race. The big race was on Saturday.

On Friday, Sam and Tom went to the store. They saw a lot of medals. Some were big and shiny. Some were small and cheap. Sam liked the big and shiny ones. Tom liked the small and cheap ones. Sam said, "I want a big and shiny medal. They are the best." Tom said, "I want a small and cheap medal. They are the best."

Sam and Tom did not agree. They went home and did not talk to each other.

On Saturday, Sam and Tom ran in the big race. They ran very fast. They passed many other kids. They were close to the finish line. Sam saw a big and shiny medal on a table. He wanted it. He ran to the table and grabbed it. He did not see the sign that said, "Do not touch."

Tom saw a small and cheap medal on a table. He wanted it. He ran to the table and grabbed it. He saw the sign that said, "First prize."

Sam and Tom crossed the finish line. Sam was happy. He had a big and shiny medal. He showed it to Tom. Tom was happy. He had a small and cheap medal. He showed it to Sam.

Sam and Tom looked at each other. They looked at their medals. They looked at the signs. They realized what happened. Sam had taken the wrong medal. Tom had taken the right medal.

Sam and Tom felt bad. They said sorry to each other. They gave back their medals. They got new medals. Sam got a small and cheap medal. Tom got a big and shiny medal.

Sam and Tom learned a lesson. They learned that medals are not important. They learned that running is fun. They learned that being friends is the best.

Sam and Tom hugged each other. They said, "We enjoy running. We enjoy our medals. We enjoy our friendship." They smiled and ran away.

Lily was a girl who liked to write poems. She had a book where she wrote her poems with a red pen. She wrote about her toys, her friends, and her family. She was very proud of her poems.

One day, she wanted to show her poems to her mom. She ran to the kitchen with her book, but she did not see the toy car on the floor. She stumbled on the car and fell down. Her book flew out of her hand and landed in the sink. The water was running and the red ink started to wash away.

Lily cried and cried. She picked up her book and saw that her poems were gone. She felt very sad and angry. She looked at the toy car and shouted, "Bad car! You ruined my poems!"

Her mom heard her cry and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily holding her wet book and the toy car on the floor. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, honey. What happened?"

Lily told her mom what happened. She said, "I wanted to show you my poems, but the car made me stumble and my book fell in the water. Now my poems are gone. They were very good poems."

Her mom kissed her and said, "I'm sure they were very good poems. I'm sorry you lost them. But you know what? You can write new poems. You have a lot of words in your head and a lot of love in your heart. You can write new poems with a new pen and a new book. And I will always listen to your poems, because I love you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you too. Can we get a new pen and a new book?"

Her mom said, "Of course we can. And maybe we can also find a new place for the toy car, so it doesn't make anyone stumble again."

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, let's do that. And then I will write a new poem for you."

Her mom said, "I can't wait to hear it."

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with her toys in her room. She did not like to talk to other kids or share her things. One day, her mom gave her a big egg for Easter. She said it was a surprise and Lily had to wait until Sunday to open it.

Lily was very curious about the egg. She wanted to see what was inside. She took the egg to her room and hid it under her bed. She thought no one would find it there. She looked at the egg every day and wondered what it was.

On Sunday, Lily woke up early and ran to her room. She wanted to open the egg before anyone else. She pulled the egg out from under her bed and started to peel off the paper. She was so excited that she did not hear her mom calling her for breakfast.

"Stop!" a voice said from inside the egg. Lily was shocked. She dropped the egg on the floor and it cracked open. Out came a fluffy yellow chick. It looked at Lily with big eyes and said, "Peep, peep!"

Lily was scared. She did not know what to do. She had never seen a real chick before. She wanted to run away, but the chick followed her. It hopped on her foot and tried to cuddle with her. It was very friendly and cute.

Lily's mom came to her room and saw the mess. She was not angry, but surprised. She explained to Lily that the egg was a special gift from her aunt, who had a farm. She said the chick was a baby chicken and needed a lot of care and love.

Lily felt sorry for breaking the egg and hurting the chick. She realized that she had been selfish and greedy. She decided to give the chick a chance and be nice to it. She named it Fluffy and hugged it gently. She also apologized to her mom and thanked her for the gift.

Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned that surprises are better when they are shared with others. She also learned that being shy is not a good reason to avoid making friends. She started to play with Fluffy and other kids in the park. She became happier and more confident. She and Fluffy were the best of friends.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their uncle Tom. Uncle Tom is playful. He makes funny faces and noises. He tickles them and chases them.

One day, uncle Tom comes to visit. He brings a big box. Anna and Ben are curious. They ask him, "What is in the box, uncle Tom?"

Uncle Tom smiles. He says, "It is a surprise. Do you want to see?"

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, yes, yes!"

Uncle Tom opens the box. He takes out a kite. It is colorful and has a long tail. He says, "This is a kite. You can fly it in the sky. Do you want to try?"

Anna and Ben clap. They say, "Yes, yes, yes!"

Uncle Tom takes them to the park. He shows them how to hold the kite and run with it. He says, "You have to let the wind catch the kite. Then it will go up, up, up!"

Anna and Ben take turns to try. They run and run. They laugh and shout. The kite flies high and low. It makes shapes in the sky. Anna and Ben are happy. They hug uncle Tom. They say, "Thank you, uncle Tom. You are the best!"

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Ben had a rod. Ben liked to make noises with his rod by hitting it on the floor and the sofa. Lily did not like the noises. They hurt her ears and made her doll cry.

"Ben, stop it!" Lily said. "You are too loud. You make me and my doll upset."

But Ben did not stop. He thought it was fun to make noises. He hit his rod harder and faster. Lily covered her ears and her doll's ears. She felt very upset.

Then, mom came into the living room. She heard the noises and saw Lily and Ben. She was not happy.

"Ben, what are you doing?" mom asked. "Why are you making so much noise? Can't you see that you are upsetting Lily and her doll?"

Ben looked at mom. He felt a little sorry. He did not mean to upset Lily and her doll. He just wanted to play.

"I'm sorry, mom. I'm sorry, Lily. I was playing with my rod. I like to make noises. But I did not know that you and your doll did not like them." Ben said.

Mom smiled. She was glad that Ben said sorry. She picked up his rod and gave him another toy. She gave him a drum and two sticks. She said, "Ben, I know you like to make noises. But you have to be careful not to hurt other people's ears. Here, you can play with this drum. It makes noises too, but they are not so loud. And you can clap with the sticks. Clapping is a nice way to make noises. Do you want to try?"

Ben nodded. He took the drum and the sticks. He clapped with the sticks. He liked the sound. It was not too loud, but it was still fun. He smiled. He said, "Thank you, mom. This is a good toy. I like to clap. Can I clap with Lily and her doll?"

Lily smiled too. She was happy that Ben said sorry and that he stopped making loud noises. She said, "Yes, you can clap with us. Clapping is fun. We can clap together and make a song. Do you want to try?"

Ben nodded. He put his drum on the floor and sat next to Lily and her doll. They clapped with their hands and their sticks. They made a song. They laughed. They had fun.

Mom watched them. She was proud of them. She said, "That's very good, Lily and Ben. You are playing nicely together. You are sharing and caring. You are making happy noises. I'm happy too."

The moral of the story is: Be careful not to hurt other people's ears with loud noises. Say sorry if you do. Clapping is a nice way to make noises and have fun. Sharing and caring make everyone happy.

Lily and Sam liked to go to the library with their mom. They could find many books with pictures and stories that they loved. They also liked to sit on the big, soft chairs and read with their mom. The chairs were very comfortable and cozy.

One day, they went to the library and saw a new book about animals. Lily wanted to read it, but so did Sam. They both reached for the book at the same time and started to pull. They did not want to share the book. They wanted to have it for themselves.

"Give me the book!" Lily said.

"No, it's mine!" Sam said.

They pulled harder and harder, until Lily got angry and pinched Sam's arm. Sam cried out and pinched Lily's cheek. Lily cried too and pinched Sam's nose. They both started to scream and cry.

Their mom heard them and came over. She was not happy. She took the book from them and put it back on the shelf. She said, "You two are being very naughty. You should not pinch each other. That hurts and is not nice. You should share and be kind. Now, we have to leave the library and go home. No more books for you today."

Lily and Sam felt sorry and sad. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't pinch again. Can we please stay and read another book?"

But their mom said, "No, you have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will behave better. Come on, let's go."

They followed their mom out of the library. They looked back at the big, soft chairs and the books they wanted to read. They wished they had not pinched each other. They wished they had shared the book. They wished they could stay in the comfortable and cozy library.

They learned that they should be nice and kind to each other and to their friends, because that is what makes them happy.

"Mom, can we go back?" Lila asked.

"No, Lila, we can't. This is our new home now. You have to accept it. I know it is hard, but you will be happy there. I promise." Mom said.

Lila did not believe mom. She did not think she could be happy on an island. She closed her eyes and wished she could go back.

After a long time, the plane landed on the island. Lila and mom got off the plane and took a bus to their new home. It was a small house near the beach. Lila saw the sea and the sand and the sun. She did not like them. She wanted to see Tom and her old home.

"Mom, I don't like it here. I want to go back." Lila said.

"Lila, please, give it a chance. You will like it here. Look, there is a playground nearby. Maybe you can find some friends there." Mom said.

Lila did not want to find some friends. She wanted to keep her old friend. She did not want to go to the playground. She wanted to go to her old home. She shook her head and ran to her new room. She locked the door and cried.

She did not know that Tom was on the same island. He and his dad had moved there too. They lived in a big house on the other side of the beach. Tom saw the sea and the sand and the sun. He liked them. He wanted to see Lila and his old home.

"Can we go to the playground, dad?" Tom asked.

"Sure, Tom, let's go. Maybe you can find some friends there." Dad said.

Tom wanted to find some friends. He wanted to keep his old friend. He wanted to go to the playground. He wanted to go to his old home. He nodded and ran to the bus with his dad.

He did not know that Lila was on the same island. He and Lila were about to meet again. They were about to be happy again. They just did not know it yet.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big balloon. It is red and yellow and blue. It is very pretty.

"Look, Jen, a balloon!" Tom says. "Can we fly with it?"

"I don't know, Tom. It looks very high. How can we fly?" Jen says.

Tom has an idea. He runs to his mom and asks for a shoe. His mom gives him a shoe. It is old and dirty. Tom does not care. He ties the shoe to the balloon with a string.

"Come on, Jen, let's fly!" Tom says. He holds the shoe and the string. He runs to the balloon. Jen follows him.

They reach the balloon. Tom jumps and grabs the balloon. Jen jumps and grabs Tom. They fly up in the air. They are very happy.

"Wow, Tom, we are flying!" Jen says. "We are so high!"

"Yes, Jen, we are flying!" Tom says. "We are like birds!"

But the balloon is not happy. It does not like the shoe. It thinks the shoe is heavy and ugly. It wants to get rid of the shoe. It pulls the string hard. The string breaks. The shoe falls down. Tom and Jen fall down too.

"Help, Tom, we are falling!" Jen says. "We are not like birds!"

"Help, Jen, we are falling!" Tom says. "We are like rocks!"

They scream and cry. They are very scared. They are very crazy.

But they are lucky. They land on a big pile of leaves. The leaves are soft and fluffy. They do not hurt. They stop screaming and crying. They laugh and hug.

"Wow, Tom, we are alive!" Jen says. "We are like cats!"

"Yes, Jen, we are alive!" Tom says. "We are like cats!"

They are very happy. They are very crazy. They do not want to fly again. They want to play with the leaves. They forget the shoe and the balloon. They are friends.

Anna did not like morning. Morning was when she had to get up and go to school. She liked school, but she liked sleeping more. She wanted to stay in her warm bed and dream of ponies and rainbows.

But her mom came to her room and said, "Anna, it's time to wake up. You have to get ready for school. You don't want to be late, do you?"

Anna frowns and pulls the blanket over her head. She says, "No, mom, I don't want to go. I want to sleep. Please, let me sleep."

Her mom smiles and says, "I know, sweetie, but you have to go. School is good for you. You learn new things and play with your friends. And you have a special day today. Do you remember what it is?"

Anna thinks for a moment and then remembers. Today is her birthday. She will have a party at school and get a cake and presents. She feels a little happy and a little excited. She says, "Oh, yes, mom, I remember. Today is my birthday. I will have a party and a cake and presents."

Her mom says, "That's right, Anna. Today is your birthday. And you know what? I have a surprise for you. Come on, get up and see."

Anna gets curious and gets up. She follows her mom to the living room. There, she sees a big box with a bow on it. Her mom says, "This is for you, Anna. Happy birthday, my love."

Anna runs to the box and opens it. Inside, she sees a beautiful doll with long hair and a pink dress. She gasps and says, "Wow, mom, thank you. She is so pretty. What is her name?"

Her mom says, "You can name her whatever you want. She is your doll. Do you like her?"

Anna hugs the doll and says, "I love her, mom. She is the best present ever. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

Her mom hugs her back and says, "You're welcome, Anna. I'm glad you like her. Now, let's get you dressed and have some breakfast. Then, we can go to school and have more fun. How does that sound?"

Anna smiles and says, "That sounds fine, mom. I'm sorry I frowns before. I like morning now. Morning is good."

Her mom says, "That's okay, Anna. I understand. Sometimes, we all frown in the morning. But then, we find something to make us smile. And today, you have many things to make you smile. Come on, let's go."

Anna nods and says, "Okay, mom. Let's go." She holds her doll and follows her mom. She thinks, "Today is a good day. Today is my birthday. I'm happy."

Lily was a little girl who liked to crawl under her bed. She had a secret spot where she kept her toys and books. She liked to pretend she was in a cave or a castle or a spaceship. Sometimes she crawled under her bed when she was scared or sad or bored.

One night, Lily heard a strange sound outside her window. It was a loud hoot, like a big horn. She crawled under her bed and grabbed her flashlight. She peeked out from under the bed and saw a big shadow on the wall. It looked like a bird with big eyes and a pointy nose. Lily was scared. She thought it was a monster.

"Who are you?" she whispered.

The shadow moved and hooted again. Lily saw that it was not a monster, but an owl. The owl was sitting on a branch near her window. It looked at her with its big eyes and tilted its head.

"I am Owl," it said. "Who are you?"

Lily was surprised. She did not know that owls could talk. She crawled out from under her bed and went to the window. She opened it a little bit and said, "I am Lily. Why are you here?"

Owl flapped its wings and said, "I am here to see the moon. It is very bright and beautiful tonight. Do you want to see it?"

Lily looked at the moon. It was big and round and shiny. She liked the moon. She nodded and said, "Yes, I want to see it. But I can't fly like you."

Owl smiled and said, "You don't have to fly. You can crawl. Crawl with me to the roof. I will show you the moon and the stars and the night."

Lily was curious. She wanted to see the night with Owl. She grabbed her flashlight and her blanket and said, "OK, I will crawl with you. But we have to be quiet. My mom and dad are sleeping."

Owl nodded and said, "OK, we will be quiet. Follow me." Owl flew to the roof and waited for Lily. Lily crawled out of the window and climbed up the gutter. She was careful not to slip or make noise. She reached the roof and saw Owl. Owl waved and said, "Come here, Lily. I have something to show you."

Lily crawled to Owl and wrapped her blanket around her. It was cold and dark on the roof. She looked at the sky and gasped. She saw the moon and the stars and the night. They were bright and beautiful and magical. She felt like she was in a dream.

Owl pointed and said, "Look, Lily. That is the Big Dipper. And that is the Little Dipper. And that is the North Star. And that is a shooting star. Make a wish, Lily. Make a wish."

Lily closed her eyes and made a wish. She wished that Owl would be her friend forever. She opened her eyes and smiled at Owl. Owl smiled back and said, "I like you, Lily. You are brave and smart and kind. You are my friend."

Lily hugged Owl and said, "I like you, too, Owl. You are wise and funny and gentle. You are my friend."

They cuddled and watched the sky. They talked and laughed and learned. They saw the moon and the stars and the night. They were happy and warm and safe.

Soon, Lily felt sleepy. She yawned and said, "Owl, I am sleepy. Can we go back to my bed?"

Owl nodded and said, "Yes, Lily. We can go back to your bed. But we will see each other again. I will come back tomorrow night. And the next night. And the next night. I will always come back to see you, Lily. You are my friend."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Owl. You are my friend, too. I will wait for you, Owl. I will always wait for you."

They crawled back to the window and said goodbye. Lily went to her bed and fell asleep. Owl flew to the branch and watched over her. They both dreamed of the moon and the stars and the night. They both dreamed of each other. They were friends.

One day, the zookeeper came to feed the octopus. He had a bucket of fish and a toy ball. He threw the ball into the tank and the octopus caught it with his arms. He squeezed it and made it squeak. Then he threw it back to the zookeeper. They did this many times and the children watched and laughed.

"Wow, he is so clever!" Tim said.

"Yes, he is. Do you want to say hello to him?" the zookeeper asked.

Tim and Mia nodded. They went closer to the glass and waved their hands. The octopus saw them and waved back with his arms. He also made a funny face and changed his color to pink.

"Hello, octopus!" Tim and Mia said.

The octopus smiled and made a bubble with his mouth. He looked happy and friendly.

But then, something happened. The ball that the zookeeper had thrown bounced off the glass and landed on the floor. It rolled away and the octopus could not see it. He looked around and became worried. He liked the ball and wanted to play more.

"Where is the ball? Where is the ball?" he said with his mouth.

Tim and Mia heard him and felt sorry for him. They wanted to help him find the ball.

"Mom, can we get the ball for the octopus?" Tim asked.

"Sure, let's go and look for it," mom said.

They followed the ball and found it near the gate. They picked it up and ran back to the tank. They showed the ball to the octopus and he was very happy. He changed his color to blue and made a big bubble.

"Thank you, thank you!" he said with his mouth.

Tim and Mia threw the ball into the tank and the octopus caught it with his arms. He squeezed it and made it squeak. Then he threw it back to them. They did this many times and the children cheered and clapped.

"Yay, octopus!" Tim and Mia said.

Lily was a small duck who lived on a farm. She liked to swim in the pond and eat bread crumbs. But she was not happy. She wanted to have a long neck like the geese who flew over the farm. She thought they looked so graceful and beautiful.

One day, she saw a goose land near the pond. She swam over to him and said, "Hello, Mr. Goose. You have a very long neck. I wish I had a neck like yours."

The goose looked at her and said, "Why do you want a long neck, little duck? You have a nice neck that suits you. A long neck is not always good. It can get in the way and cause trouble."

Lily did not listen. She said, "No, I want a long neck. It would make me happy. How can I get a long neck like yours?"

The goose said, "Well, there is a way, but it is not easy. You have to stretch your neck every day, as much as you can. And you have to eat a lot of grass and leaves, not bread crumbs. If you do this for a long time, maybe your neck will grow longer."

Lily was excited. She said, "Thank you, Mr. Goose. I will do that. Goodbye." She swam away and started to stretch her neck and eat grass and leaves.

She did this for many days and weeks. She did not swim with her friends or eat bread crumbs. She only stretched her neck and ate grass and leaves. She thought her neck was getting longer, but it was not. It was only getting thinner and weaker.

One day, a fox came to the farm. He saw Lily by the pond, stretching her neck and eating grass and leaves. He thought, "What a tasty snack. She has a long, thin neck that I can easily bite. I will catch her and eat her."

He crept closer and closer to Lily, who did not see him. She was too busy stretching her neck and eating grass and leaves. When he was close enough, he jumped out and grabbed her neck with his teeth.

Lily screamed and tried to get away, but it was too late. Her neck was too weak to resist. The fox dragged her to his den and ate her.

The moral of the story is: Be happy with what you have. Do not try to be something you are not. You may lose what makes you special and put yourself in danger.

One day, her mom said, "Sara, you need to change your dress. It is too old and too small for you. I have a new dress for you. It is blue and pretty. You will like it."

Sara did not want to change her dress. She said, "No, mom. I want to wear my pink dress. It is my dress. I love it."

Her mom said, "Sara, you can't wear your pink dress forever. It is not good for you. It is not clean or comfortable. It is not nice to others. You have to try new things sometimes. Trust me, you will like the blue dress. It is also your dress. I made it for you."

Her mom sighed. She said, "Sara, I understand you love your pink dress. But you have to grow up and learn to let go of old things. You have to be brave and curious and open to new things. The moral of the story is: You should listen to your mom and try new things. You should not be afraid of change or cling to old things. You should appreciate what you have and what you get. You should love your mom and yourself.

"Wow, that's cool, Max! I have a cross screw!" Lily said, holding a screw with a cross-shaped head.

"Look, Lily, I made a monster face!" Max said, showing his paper with a big star screw eye and a cross screw mouth.

"Look, Max, I made a princess face!" Lily said, showing her paper with two cross screw eyes and a star screw nose.

They were very proud of their creative faces and wanted to show them to their mom and dad. They picked up their papers and ran to the kitchen. But they forgot to close the box of screws. As they ran, some of the screws fell out of the box and scattered on the floor. They made a loud noise and a mess.

"What are you doing, Lily and Max?" their mom asked.

They were happy to see their children having fun and learning new things.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big iron in the closet. It was shiny and heavy and had a long cord. Ben wanted to touch it, but Sam said no.

"Stop, Ben! That is not a toy. It is hot and can hurt you. Mom uses it to make clothes smooth. We should prevent you from getting burned. Let's play with something else."

But Ben did not listen. He was curious and stubborn. He pulled the iron out of the closet and plugged it in the wall. He saw a red light on the iron and felt some heat. He smiled and reached for the iron.

Suddenly, a loud bark made him jump. It was Rex, their hairy dog. Rex saw Ben playing with the iron and ran to him. He pushed Ben away with his nose and knocked the iron off the table. The iron fell on the floor and broke. The cord sparked and smoked.

"Rex, no!" Ben cried. He was scared and angry. He tried to hit Rex, but Sam stopped him.

"Ben, Rex saved you. He is a good dog. He prevented you from touching the iron and getting burned. You should be thankful and kind to him. He loves you and wants you to be safe."

Ben looked at Rex, who wagged his tail and licked his face. He felt sorry and ashamed. He hugged Rex and said sorry.

"Sorry, Rex. You are a good dog. Thank you for preventing me from getting hurt. I love you too. And sorry, Sam. You were right. The iron is not a toy. I should have listened to you."

Sam smiled and hugged Ben and Rex. He said sorry too.

"Sorry, Mom. We broke your iron. We were playing with it and it was a bad idea. We learned our lesson. We will not touch it again."

Mom came home and saw the broken iron and the boys and the dog. She was upset and sad, but also relieved and proud.

"Boys, I am upset and sad that you broke my iron. It was expensive and useful. You should not play with it. It is dangerous and can hurt you. But I am also relieved and proud that you are okay. You learned your lesson and said sorry. And Rex, you are a hero. You prevented a disaster and protected the boys. You are a good dog. I love you all."

She hugged the boys and the dog and gave them a kiss. She said they would have to buy a new iron and be more careful next time. She also said they would have to do something nice for Rex, like giving him a treat or a toy. The boys agreed and said they loved her too. They learned that playing with the iron was a bad idea, that listening to their brother and their dog was a good idea, and that saying sorry and being thankful was a nice thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate fox who was searching for trouble. Everywhere she looked, she only saw gentle things. But then one day, she saw a big ball nearby. With a twinkle in her eye, she gave it a kick! The fox was so happy! The gentle ball rolled away, leading her to more and more trouble. 

The fox kicked and kicked the ball, until it rolled down a deep hill. Suddenly, the fox found herself in a big meadow full of adventure! She ran and kicked the ball and laughed and smiled, until something unexpected happened. 

The delicate fox stumbled into a thorn bush! She yelped and quickly pulled herself free. But the fox was unharmed and with a smile, she kicked the ball even higher into the sky. And when she did, the fox found a wonderful surprise. 

A flock of birds filled the sky! They sang and danced and soared through the air. The fox watched in awe and wonder, until she heard a familiar sound. A gentle kick from the ball. A reminder of the trouble she still sought.

Once there was a baby elephant who was fearful of the world around him. He was so scared that he would find an escape. Every day he looked but he never found one. One day, as he was looking around, he saw a small door. He went up and paid attention to it.

He looked closely and saw that this door could take him away. He pushed on the door and it opened. He was so excited and started to run away. But then he was stopped by someone.
It was an old man. He said, "You have to pay to escape."
The baby elephant did not understand, so he just nodded his head and said, "I'll give you all my money." He pulled out some peanuts from his pocket and gave them to the old man.

The old man smiled and said, "You can go now." The baby elephant was so relieved, he hurried off and was never scared anymore. He was so happy now and he found an escape! He was free!

Once there was a leopard who lived in the forest. Every day, the leopard would run through the trees, feeling free and happy. He wanted to explore the world around him.

One day, the leopard decided something different. He stayed still in one spot and closed his eyes. He was so still that he felt like he was frozen in place. The birds in the trees sang his name and the sun shone down on him.

The leopard stayed there for a long time and felt so peaceful. Suddenly, he felt something soft and furry brush against his legs. It was a small kitten. The leopard looked down and saw that the kitten was trying to curl around him. He made sure to stay still so he wouldn't scare the little animal away.

The leopard froze in place as the kitten purred softly. Finally the kitten got up and the leopard opened his eyes. That day the leopard learned the power of stillness. He would never forget the soft feel of the kitten's fur on his legs.

Once upon a time there was a big, blue bear. He was very attractive and liked to go for walks in the park. One day he saw a law on the ground and he wanted to pick it up and read it. He bent down and carefully squeezed the law between his furry fingers. But when he tried to let go, the law wouldn't come out of his hand! He squeezed it even harder and it made a loud popping noise. Now the law was stuck to his paw! The bear was so smooth that it was difficult for anyone to grab the law and take it away. So he kept it there, and it became a fun accessory for the bear! Everywhere he went, he showed off his law that he had squeezed so tightly. The bear was very proud of his attractive law and kept it with him forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who didn't like to do what her parents said. She wanted to do what she wanted to do. Everyday her parents asked her to clean her room, but she didn't want to. She tried to resist.

One day when she was feeling particularly strong and brave, she decided to not listen to her parents and went to the window to look out. From her view she could see a lovely garden full of different kinds of trees, plants and flowers.

But then something unexpected happened. She saw a very weak bee flitting about the garden, looking for nectar but not finding any. The little girl felt very sorry for the bee and knew she had to help it.

Suddenly, her need to resist her parents was gone and she raced to clean her room. She wanted to help the bee so badly that she forgot all about her earlier desire to resist.

"Goodbye, dragon. Thank you for your story. See you tomorrow," Lily says. She closes the book and puts it on her bed. She runs downstairs to join her mother. She is happy. She has a new friend. A dragon friend.

"Yes, come on!" Lily says. They run to Lily's room and take out their toys. They have fun making stories with the dolls and cars.

But then, Lily's mother hears a loud noise. She goes to Lily's room and sees a big mess. The toys are everywhere. Some are broken. The juice and cookies are spilled on the bed and the floor.

"What are you doing?" Lily's mother asks. She is angry. "You are bad children! You made a big mess and broke the toys! You have to clean up and say sorry!"

Lily and Tom are scared. They did not mean to be bad. They were just playing. They start to cry.

"We are sorry, mother," Lily says. "We did not want to be bad. We were just playing."

"Playing is good, but you have to be careful and respectful," Lily's mother says. "You have to take care of your toys and your room. You have to listen to me and follow the rules. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nod. They say sorry again. They help Lily's mother clean up the mess. They hug and say they are sorry. Lily's mother is not angry anymore. She is glad they learned their lesson. She tells them they can play again, but they have to be good. Lily and Tom agree. They smile and hug. They are still friends. They are happy.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big cow in the field next to their house. The cow was brown and white and had a bell around its neck.

"Let's go and say hello to the cow!" Ben said.

"Okay!" Lily said.

They ran to the fence and climbed over it. The cow looked at them and mooed. Ben and Lily walked closer to the cow and tried to pet it. The cow was soft and warm.

"Hello, cow! You are very nice!" Ben said.

"Moo!" the cow said.

Lily saw something shiny on the cow's bell. She reached out to touch it. But she was too small and slipped off the cow's back. She fell to the ground and hurt her knee.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Lily cried.

Ben heard Lily and ran to help her. He saw blood on her knee and felt scared.

"Lily, are you okay?" Ben asked.

"No, Ben, it hurts!" Lily said.

Ben did not know what to do. He felt helpless. He looked around and saw their house. He shouted for their mom.

"Mom! Mom! Help! Lily is hurt!" Ben shouted.

Mom heard Ben and came out of the house. She saw Ben and Lily in the field with the cow. She ran to them and picked up Lily.

"What happened?" Mom asked.

"Lily fell off the cow and hurt her knee!" Ben said.

Mom looked at Lily's knee and saw a small cut. She cleaned it with a cloth and put a band-aid on it.

"There, there, Lily. You'll be fine. It's just a scratch." Mom said.

"Thank you, Mom. You are the best!" Lily said.

Mom hugged Lily and smiled. She looked at Ben and said, "You are a good brother, Ben. You tried to help Lily and called me. I'm proud of you."

"Thank you, Mom. I love you!" Ben said.

Mom hugged Ben and said, "I love you too. Now, let's go back to the house and have some cookies. And say goodbye to the cow."

"Goodbye, cow! Thank you for letting us pet you!" Ben and Lily said.

"Moo!" the cow said.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. Lily has a big red truck. Ben has a small blue car. They pretend to drive on the road.

"Beep beep!" Ben says. "Move your truck, Lily. I want to go fast."

"No, Ben. This is my road. You have to wait," Lily says. She likes to be the boss.

Ben is not happy. He wants to play fair. He has an idea. He says, "Lily, do you have a license for your truck?"

"A license? What is that?" Lily asks.

"A license is a paper that says you can drive. You need a license to drive on the road. I have a license for my car. See?" Ben shows Lily a card with his name and picture on it. He made it with crayons.

Lily looks at the card. She thinks it is pretty. She says, "Wow, Ben. That is a nice license. Can I have one too?"

"Sure, Lily. I can make you one. But you have to be gentle with my car. And you have to share the road with me. OK?" Ben says.

"OK, Ben. That sounds fair. Thank you for making me a license. You are a good friend," Lily says.

They hug and smile. Then they play with their cars and trucks. They are gentle and share the road. They have fun.

Lily and Tom were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build tall towers and knock them down. They laughed and had fun.

Suddenly, the floor shook and the blocks fell. The lamps and pictures swung and rattled. Lily and Tom felt scared. They did not know what was happening. They heard a loud noise outside.

"It's an earthquake!" their mom shouted from the kitchen. "Come here, quick!"

Lily and Tom ran to their mom. She hugged them and took them under the table. She told them to stay calm and wait for the shaking to stop.

The earthquake lasted for a few minutes. Then it was quiet. Lily and Tom felt anxious. They wondered if their house and toys were okay. They hoped no one was hurt.

Their mom checked the radio and the phone. She said the earthquake was not very big and there was no damage in their area. She said they were lucky and safe.

She took Lily and Tom outside to see the sky and the trees. She said they should be thankful for what they have and help others who might need it.

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt better. They said they loved their mom and each other. They learned that earthquakes are scary, but they can be brave and kind.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a shiny red bike near the fence. It had a big handle and a bell that made a loud noise. Lily and Tom wanted to ride the bike, but they did not know who it belonged to.

"Let's go and see the bike," Lily said to Tom. "Maybe we can take turns."

Tom nodded and followed Lily. They ran to the fence and climbed over it. They reached the bike and gazed at it with wonder. It looked so fun and fast.

Lily grabbed the handle and tried to get on the bike. But it was too big for her. She fell down and scraped her knee. She cried out in pain.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Tom asked. He helped her get up and hugged her.

Lily sniffed and nodded. She looked at the bike again. She still wanted to ride it.

"Maybe you can try, Tom," she said. "You are bigger than me."

Tom hesitated. He was scared of falling too. But he also wanted to try the bike. He nodded and got on the bike. He pushed the pedals and rang the bell. He felt happy and proud.

But then, he heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing with my bike?" It was Ben, the boy who lived next door. He was angry and ran towards them.

Lily and Tom were scared. They knew they had been naughty. They had taken Ben's bike without asking. They jumped off the bike and ran back to the fence. They climbed over it and ran to their house.

They did not look back at Ben or the bike. They felt sorry and ashamed. They decided to never take things that were not theirs again. They learned their lesson.

Ben and Lily were twins. They liked to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they did not like to share. They wanted the same thing.

One day, they went to the park with Mom. Mom said they could ride the swings and the slide. Ben and Lily were happy. They ran to the swings. But there were only two swings. And both of them wanted the blue swing.

"I want the blue swing!" Ben said.

"No, I want the blue swing!" Lily said.

They both ran to the blue swing. They tried to sit on it. But they did not fit. They pushed and pulled. They started to fight.

"Stop it, Ben and Lily!" Mom said. "You can't both have the same swing. You have to take turns. Or you can use the other swing. It is red. Red is a nice color too."

"But I don't like red!" Ben said.

"Me neither!" Lily said.

They did not listen to Mom. They kept fighting. They made a lot of noise. They made the other kids sad.

Then, a big boy came. He was older than Ben and Lily. He saw them fighting. He did not like it. He walked to the blue swing. He pushed Ben and Lily away. He sat on the swing. He smiled.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Ben said.

"That's our swing!" Lily said.

They tried to get the swing back. But the big boy was too strong. He swung higher and higher. He laughed.

"Ha ha, this is my swing now!" he said.

Ben and Lily felt bad. They looked at Mom. Mom looked at them. She shook her head.

"See, this is what happens when you don't share. You lose what you want. And you make someone else happy. Is that what you want?" Mom said.

Ben and Lily thought about it. They did not want to lose the swing. They did not want to make the big boy happy. They wanted to have fun. They wanted to be nice.

They looked at each other. They nodded. They said sorry to each other. They hugged.

"Mom, can we use the red swing?" Ben said.

"Yes, we can. And we can take turns. And we can say thank you. And we can make friends." Lily said.

Mom smiled. She was proud of Ben and Lily. She took them to the red swing. They sat on it. They fit. They swung together. They said thank you. They made friends with the other kids. They had fun.

The end.

Sara and Tom were twins who loved to gaze at the stars. Every night, they would sneak out of their beds and go to the window. They would point at the bright dots and make up stories about them. They wished they could fly up and see them closer.

One day, their mom told them they were going on a trip. She said they would stay in a big house with a pool and a garden. Sara and Tom were very excited. They thought it would be a luxury to have so much fun. They packed their bags and got in the car.

The trip was long and boring. Sara and Tom fell asleep in the back seat. When they woke up, they saw a lot of trees and hills. They did not see any big house or pool or garden. They saw a sign that said "Wild Camp". Their mom smiled and said, "Surprise! We're going camping!"

Sara and Tom did not like the surprise. They did not want to sleep in a tent or eat beans or use a hole for a toilet. They wanted to go back to their home and their beds and their window. They started to cry and complain.

Their mom tried to cheer them up. She said camping was an adventure. She said they would see animals and flowers and fireflies. She said they would still gaze at the stars, but even better. She said they would have stories to tell when they got back.

Sara and Tom did not believe her. They thought camping was a nightmare. They did not want any adventure. They wanted their luxury. They did not know that their mom had a plan. She had a special gift for them. She had a telescope.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to swim in the pool. They both learned how to do tricks in the water, like jumping, spinning, and diving. They had fun showing each other their tricks and cheering for each other.

One day, a new kid came to the pool. His name was Max, and he said he was the best swimmer in the world. He said he could do any trick better than Lily and Ben, and he wanted to perform for everyone. He was not very nice, and he made fun of Lily and Ben's tricks.

Lily and Ben felt sad and angry, but they did not want to fight with Max. They decided to ignore him and keep swimming. They said to each other, "We don't need to show off. We just need to have fun and be kind."

Max did not like that Lily and Ben did not pay attention to him. He wanted to impress them and make them jealous. He tried to do a very hard trick, but he did not practice enough. He jumped too high, spun too fast, and hit his head on the edge of the pool. He cried out in pain and fear.

Lily and Ben heard him and ran to help him. They called for the lifeguard and stayed with him until he was safe. They asked him if he was okay and told him not to worry. They were not mad at him, even though he was mean to them.

Max felt sorry for what he did and said. He realized that Lily and Ben were good friends and good swimmers. He thanked them for helping him and apologized for being rude. He learned that being modest and respectful is better than being boastful and arrogant. He asked them if they could be friends and teach him some tricks. They agreed and smiled.

The moral of the story is: Don't be a show-off. Be humble and kind.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big object near the trees. It was shiny and round. They wanted to see what it was.

"Let's go, Ben!" Lily said. "Maybe it is a ball or a toy."

"OK, Lily!" Ben said. "But be careful. It might be something bad."

"Wow, what is this?" Lily asked. She touched a button.

"Don't touch it, Lily!" Ben shouted. "It might be dangerous!"

But it was too late. The button made a loud noise. The object started to beep and flash. Ben and Lily realized they had made a big mistake. They tried to run away, but they were too slow.

The object exploded. It made a very loud noise and a big fire. Ben and Lily were hurt. They screamed and cried. Nobody heard them. Nobody helped them. They were alone and scared. The end.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with blocks. They liked to build tall towers and see who could make the highest one. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes, but they only had one red block. The red block was their favorite, because it was big and shiny and had a number on it. The number was six.

One day, they decided to have a contest to see who could use the red block to make the highest tower. They each took some blocks and started to build on opposite sides of the room. Tim was fast and used many blocks to make a wide base. Sam was slow and used few blocks to make a narrow base. He wanted to save the red block for the top.

"Look at my tower, Sam!" Tim said. "It is almost as high as the table. I will win for sure!"

Sam did not say anything. He just smiled and kept building. He made his tower higher and higher, until it was as high as the table. Then he took the red block and put it on the top. His tower was now higher than Tim's.

"Look at my tower, Tim!" Sam said. "It is higher than yours. I win!"

Tim was angry. He ran to Sam's tower and tried to knock it down. But Sam was wise and had made his tower strong. It did not fall. Instead, Tim's tower fell and made a loud noise. The noise made their mom come to the room.

"What are you doing, boys?" she asked. "Why are you making such a mess?"

Tim and Sam looked at their mom. They looked at the blocks. They looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they had done.

"We were playing with the blocks, mom," Tim said. "We wanted to see who could make the highest tower with the red block."

"The red block?" mom asked. "You mean this one?" She picked up the red block and showed it to them. "This is not a block, boys. This is a calculator. It has numbers on it, but it can also do math. See?" She pressed some buttons and showed them the screen. "Six plus six is twelve. Twelve is a bigger number than six."

Tim and Sam were amazed. They did not know that the red block could do math. They wanted to learn more.

"Can you teach us how to use it, mom?" Sam asked.

"Of course, I can," mom said. "But first, you have to clean up the blocks and say sorry to each other. Then we can have some fun with the calculator."

Tim and Sam nodded. They hugged each other and said sorry. Then they cleaned up the blocks and went to mom. They learned how to use the calculator and had fun with the numbers. They realized that the red block was not only their favorite, but also their most useful. They decided to share it and use it together. They were happy.

"Rex, come back!" Tim shouted. He ran after his dog. But he was too slow. The big dog caught Rex and bit him hard. Rex yelped and whimpered. Tim reached them and tried to pull the big dog away. But the big dog was too strong. He shook Rex and threw him to the ground. Rex did not move.

"Rex, Rex, wake up!" Tim cried. He hugged his dog and sobbed. Mom came and saw what happened. She was sad and angry. She called the big dog's owner and the vet. But it was too late. Rex was gone.

Tim was very sad. He missed his dog. He wished he had been more thoughtful. He wished he had kept Rex on his leash. He wished he had saved him. He wished he had his best friend back.

Tom and Sue jumped off the rock and ran to their mother. She sprayed some cream on their bites and hugged them. They felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had been selfish and rude. They had ignored the beauty of nature and the love of their parents.

"Mom, Dad, we are sorry. We were bad. We did not appreciate what you did for us. We did not enjoy the forest. We only wanted our things. Can you forgive us?" they said, looking at their parents with tears in their eyes.

Their parents smiled and kissed them. They forgave them and told them they loved them. They said they were glad they learned their lesson. They said they hoped they would be more grateful and happy from now on.

They finished their picnic and went for a walk around the lake. They saw a duck and her ducklings, a squirrel and a nut, a butterfly and a flower. They laughed and played and talked. They felt a new joy and peace in their hearts. They thanked their parents and the forest for their wonderful day. Do not open!" But Tom was curious and did not listen. He opened the box and saw a lot of wires and buttons.

He was a soldier and had to defuse the bomb, but he had not done it yet. The bomb started to beep and flash. Tom was scared and tried to close the box, but it was too late.

The bomb exploded and made a loud noise. It hurt Tom and his dad, who ran to the garage when he heard the beeping. They both fell to the ground and did not get up. The garage was on fire and the house was damaged. Tom's mom and sister came out and saw the smoke and the blood. They cried and called for help, but it was too late.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch things that are not yours, especially if they have a sign that says "Danger!" You could get in trouble or hurt yourself and others. Listen to your parents and be careful. Curiosity is good, but not when it is foolish.

Ben and Lily were two frogs who lived in a swamp. They liked to hop and swim and catch flies. One day, they saw a big bird flying over the swamp. It had a long neck and a sharp beak. It was a heron.

"Look, Ben, a heron!" Lily said. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Yes, it is," Ben said. "But we have to be careful. Herons like to eat frogs."

They hid under a water lily and watched the heron. The heron landed on a log and looked around. It saw a fish in the water and snapped it up. Then it saw a snake on the shore and grabbed it. Then it saw a mouse in the grass and caught it.

"Wow, the heron is so hungry!" Lily said. "It eats everything!"

"Yes, it does," Ben said. "But it does not eat humble frogs like us. We are too small and plain."

They felt proud of being humble frogs. They decided to rest on the log and enjoy the sun. They hopped out of the water and climbed on the log. They did not see the heron behind them. The heron saw them and opened its beak.

"Hello, humble frogs," the heron said. "You look like a tasty snack."

Ben and Lily were scared. They jumped off the log and back into the water. They swam away as fast as they could. They did not rest on the log again.

When it was time to return home, Tom put the interesting toast back on his plate. He smiled as he thought about the fun day he had with his friends. Tom knew that tomorrow, he would have another great day with his interesting toast.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big computer in his room. It was dark outside, and Tim wanted to play with the computer. He turned it on and saw many fun things on the screen. Tim was very happy.

As Tim played, he saw a game about counting. He wanted to learn how to count, so he clicked on the game. The game had a friendly voice that said, "Hi, Tim! Let's count together!" Tim smiled and said, "Okay!"

Together, Tim and the voice counted from one to ten. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" Tim felt proud that he could count. He played the game until it was time for bed. When his mom came in to say goodnight, Tim told her, "Mom, I can count now!" His mom hugged him and said, "I'm so proud of you, Tim!"

Fluffy's friend, a little dog named Spot, saw the ashtray too. Spot did not know it was not a toy. He tried to play with it, but it made him cough and feel bad. Fluffy saw this and wanted to help her friend. She thought hard about what to do.

One icy day, Tim and Mr. Bones went outside to play. They could hear the wind blowing in the trees. Mr. Bones said, "Brrr, it's cold!" Tim laughed and said, "Yes, it is! Let's play a game to stay warm."

So, Tim and Mr. Bones played hide-and-seek. Tim closed his eyes and counted. Mr. Bones went to hide. Tim looked and looked for Mr. Bones, but he could not find him. Then, Tim heard a sound. It was Mr. Bones! He found him hiding behind a big tree.

Tim and Mr. Bones played all day in the icy cold. When they were tired, they went inside to get warm. They had hot cocoa and talked about their fun day. Tim and Mr. Bones were very happy.

Finally, they found the bird's home. The bird was very happy and thanked the mouse. The mouse felt good about helping the bird. The moral of the story is to always help others, even when it's hard.

Tom decided to step on Max's tail to make him run away, so he could take the diamond. Max cried out and ran, but he did not know why Tom did that. Max was very sad and did not understand why his friend would hurt him.

Tom took the diamond, but he soon felt bad for what he did. He went to Max and said sorry. He gave the diamond back to Max, and they were friends again. The moral of the story is that it is not nice to be naughty and take things that do not belong to you. It is better to be kind and share with your friends.

To make Lily feel better, her mom took her outside to see the distant mountains. Lily loved looking at the big mountains and it made her forget about her onion tears. From then on, Lily always helped measure ingredients for dinner and loved looking at the distant mountains with her mom. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a farm with lots of sheep. One day, a mysterious sheep appeared. It was different from the others, with a special pattern on its wool. The other sheep were curious and went to see it, but some of them started to tease the mysterious sheep. 

The mysterious sheep felt sad and didn't understand why they were being mean. It just wanted to be friends with them. But the teasing continued, until a little girl arrived at the farm. She saw the mysterious sheep and thought it was beautiful. 

She went to talk to it and the sheep felt happy. The little girl petted its wool and gave it some food. From that day on, the mysterious sheep had a friend and the other sheep learned to be kind and not tease anymore. They all lived happily ever after.

Benny went to his friend, the rabbit, to borrow a scale. He needed to weigh his bag to make sure it wasn't too heavy. The rabbit was happy to help and lent Benny the scale.

Benny went on his trip and found a peaceful spot by the river. He sat down and had a picnic with his food. He played with his toys and enjoyed the peaceful surroundings. Benny was happy he packed everything he needed for his trip.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing in the garden. One day, she saw a big sunflower and wanted to pick it. But her mom said, "No, Lily. That flower is too dangerous. It has thorns that can hurt you."

Lily was sad, but she listened to her mom and went to play with her toys instead. Later that day, Lily's friend Jack came over to play. Jack liked to tease Lily and said, "I bet you're too scared to go near that sunflower."

Lily remembered what her mom had said and didn't want to get hurt. But Jack kept teasing her, so she decided to show him she wasn't scared. She walked over to the sunflower, but as she reached out to touch it, she felt a prick on her finger.

Suddenly, Lily remembered her mom's warning and ran back to her house. Her mom saw her crying and asked what happened. Lily told her about the sunflower and her mom hugged her, saying, "I'm so glad you listened to me. It's important to stay safe and not let others tease you into doing something dangerous."

"Mommy, can I play with them too?" Lily asked.

Her mom replied, "Of course, but you need to use your shoes to keep your feet safe."

Lily quickly put on her shoes and joined the other kids. They were all very playful and had a lot of fun together. After a while, Lily's mom called her over and said, "Remember, it's important to always use your shoes when you play outside. They protect your feet and keep you safe."

Lily nodded and smiled, happy to have learned something new. From that day on, she always made sure to wear her shoes when she went outside to play.

Sally said, "Yes, please!"

The wise owl knew just what to do. He told the duckling to follow him and they went on a big adventure through the forest. They saw many animals along the way, but none of them were the duckling's mommy. Finally, they found a pond where the duckling's mommy was waiting for him. The mommy duck was very happy to see her baby and thanked the wise owl for his help. 

From that day on, the wise owl and the duckling became good friends. They would often meet by the river and enjoy oat cookies together. The owl was happy to have made a new friend and the duckling was grateful for the wise owl's help.

Lily and Tom were playing a game. They had to find things that were dry in the garden. Lily found a leaf, a stick and a stone. Tom found a feather, a shell and a flower. They put their things in a basket.

"Who has more things?" Lily asked.

"Let's count them," Tom said. They counted their things. Lily had three things. Tom had three things too.

"It's a tie," Tom said. "We both win."

"No, I win," Lily said. "My things are better than yours. Your flower is not dry. It is wet."

Tom looked at his flower. It was wet from the rain. He felt sad. He liked his flower.

"That's not fair," Tom said. "You can't change the rules. We were looking for dry things, not better things."

"I don't care," Lily said. "I win and you lose. I get the prize."

"What prize?" Tom asked.

Lily pointed to a big cookie on the table. "That prize. Mommy said we can have it if we play nicely."

Tom was angry. He hated Lily. She was mean and selfish. He wanted the cookie too.

He grabbed the basket and dumped all their things on the ground. He ran to the table and took the cookie. He broke it in half and gave one half to Lily.

"Here," he said. "You can have this half. It's dry and hard and yucky. I'll have this half. It's soft and sweet and yummy."

He took a big bite of his half of the cookie. He smiled.

Lily looked at her half of the cookie. It was dry and hard and yucky. She felt sorry. She was mean and selfish. She wanted to share the cookie with Tom.

She ran to Tom and gave him her half of the cookie. "I'm sorry," she said. "You can have this half. It's dry and hard and yucky. I'll have this half. It's soft and sweet and yummy."

She took a big bite of her half of the cookie. She smiled.

Tom looked at her half of the cookie. It was soft and sweet and yummy. He felt happy. He liked Lily. She was nice and generous. He wanted to share the cookie with Lily.

He gave her back her half of the cookie. "Thank you," he said. "You can have this half. It's soft and sweet and yummy. I'll have this half. It's dry and hard and yucky."

They both laughed. They ate their halves of the cookie. They hugged.

They were friends again.

One day, she saw an elderly lady sitting on a bench in the park. The lady had white hair and a kind face. She smiled at Ella and said, "Hello, little girl. Do you like bubbles?"

Ella nodded and ran to the lady. She showed her the bottle and the wand and said, "Look, I can make bubbles. Do you want to try?"

The lady took the wand and blew gently. A big bubble came out and drifted towards Ella. Ella clapped and laughed. She reached out to touch the bubble, but it burst with a pop.

"Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to break your bubble," the lady said.

Ella shook her head and said, "It's okay. Bubbles are fun. They make me happy."

Ella shook her head and said, "No, I'm not cold. I'm happy. You make me happy. You are my friend."

The lady hugged Ella and said, "You make me happy too. You are my friend. Thank you for sharing your bubbles with me."

They smiled and cuddled and blew more bubbles together. They felt warm and cozy and happy. They were friends.

One day, they went to the zoo with their mom and dad. They saw the lions, the monkeys, the elephants, and the giraffes. They also saw a new animal that they did not know. It had a long nose, big ears, and a lot of hair. It was gray and brown.

"What is that?" Sara asked.

"Yes, please!" Sara and Ben said.

They followed the zoo keeper to the llama's cage. They used a big broom to sweep the dirt and the poop. They used a hose to spray water and make it wet. They used a bucket to bring fresh hay and grass. They also gave the llama a carrot as a treat.

The llama was happy and made a funny sound. It sounded like a hum. Sara and Ben laughed and petted its soft hair.

"Thank you for helping me," the zoo keeper said. "You are very good at cleaning. The llama likes you too. Do you want to give it a name?"

Sara and Ben thought for a moment. They looked at the llama's nose, ears, and hair. They had an idea.

"Let's call it Nelly," they said.

Nelly hummed again and licked Sara and Ben's faces. They giggled and hugged Nelly.

They had a lot of fun at the zoo. They learned about a different animal and made a new friend. They also helped to keep the zoo clean and happy.

Mom came home and saw the wall. She saw some faint traces of the drawing, but she also saw Anna and Ben smiling at her. She knew they had tried to fix their mistake. She smiled back and said, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. But next time, please draw on paper, not on the wall. Okay?"

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to pay a price. You have to help me with the dishes tonight."

Anna and Ben said, "Okay, mom. We will help you with the dishes."

They went to the kitchen and helped mom with the dishes. They were happy and proud. They had learned a lesson and made up with each other. They had paid the price and earned mom's love.

He ran down the road, looking around and sniffing the air. Soon, he smelled something smelly. He followed the smell and saw a small hole. He decided to go in.

When he got inside, he was surprised by what he saw. It was dark, but he could just make out something round and grey moving around in the corner. He moved closer and saw that it was a skunk! Jack was scared but the skunk smiled and said, "Hi Jack, I'm Manny. Don't be scared. I won't show you any harm."

Manny then proceeded to show Jack around his home, teaching him about all the different things he could find there. Jack had a fun time and was surprised by all the different cool things he saw.

At the end of his visit, Manny said to Jack, "Remember, Jack. There is no harm in exploring. You can always go back when you feel scared!" Jack thanked Manny and waved goodbye. 

As Jack went home he remembered Manny's words. He knew he would return one day, with new courage and ready for more adventures.

"It's a hurricane," said Mommy. "We have to be tough and prepare for the storm."

Marta and Mommy worked hard to board up the windows and secure the furniture. As the storm passed, Marta was still worried about the damage it might have caused.

Mommy held her close and said, "We are tough, and we can make it through the storm. Everything will be okay."

Marta felt safe in Mommy's arms, and she knew that Mommy was right. Together, they were tougher than any hurricane.

The man was glad to remain safe, but he was sad to see his boat stay in the wreck. He said a silent goodbye to the boat, each time he looked at the shore.

The boat stayed in the wreck, all alone and light, but the man was glad to remain safe on the shore.

The wind stopped whistling and the flower went back to standing still. But then a thought came to the flower. It thought that maybe it should try whistling like the wind.

The flower tried very hard but couldn't get the whistling right. No matter how hard it tried, the whistling was never quite right.

The flower decided it would never be able to whistle like the wind. But it was still happy and very healthy. So it just enjoyed swaying in the wind and watching the other flowers.

On a warm summer's day three robots walked towards the park. The robots were all very independent and varied in size.

The first robot marched quickly and had wheels instead of feet. It zoomed past the others and was the fastest robot around.

The second robot marched carefully in between the trees. Its big metal feet clanked against the ground and it carried a big bag filled with goodies.

The third robot marched slowly, but proudly. It's brightly coloured wings shone in the sunlight as it flapped them gently every now and then to stay afloat.

The three robots arrived at the park and had lots of fun. They raced around and played tag with each other. As the sun set, the robots waved goodbye and began their march home.

"Be careful, Lily. Spiders can bite," Mommy replied.

Suddenly, the spider struck at Lily, but she was too quick and jumped out of the way. 

"Wow, you're so fast, Lily!" Mommy said.

The spider crawled away and they continued shopping. As they were leaving, they saw a dead bug on the ground.

"Eww, a dead bug!" Lily said.

"Yes, it's not very nice to see dead things," Mommy replied.

Lily nodded her head and they went home with their groceries.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They lived in a big house with modern furniture. One day, the parents had a big fight and decided to separate. The children didn't understand what was happening and felt very sad.

The father moved to a different house and the children missed him very much. But whenever they went to visit him, he always gave them a warm welcome and made them feel loved. The mother, on the other hand, was always angry and didn't want the children to see their father.

One day, the mother got sick and had to go to the hospital. The children wanted to visit her, but the father didn't let them because he was still angry at the mother. The children felt very conflicted and didn't know what to do. In the end, they learned that even when people separate, they should still be kind to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, she saw a turkey outside. It was wet and looked sad.

Lily said, "Oh no! Poor turkey. It must be suffering in the rain. I will help it."

Lily went inside and got a towel. She went back outside and wrapped the turkey in the towel. The turkey felt warm and dry.

"Thank you, Lily," said the turkey. "You are very kind."

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, turkey. I don't like to see anyone suffer, even animals."

"We have to leave now! The dog is too big and he might hurt us," said Freddy.
