Once upon a time, there was a frog named Fred. Fred was a modest frog who liked to hide in the pond. One day, Fred saw a big frog who was bragging to all the other frogs about how fast he could jump. 

Fred said to the big frog, "Why do you brag so much? It's not nice." 

The big frog replied, "I'm the best and everyone should know it." 

Fred thought for a moment and then said, "I may not jump as high as you, but I can hide better than anyone. Being modest is better than bragging." 

The big frog realized that Fred was right and apologized for his behavior. From that day on, the big frog learned to be modest and the two frogs became good friends. The moral of the story is that it's better to be modest and kind than to brag and be mean.

Suddenly, Lily saw a mess in the park. She pointed at it and said, "Look! We need to clean that up." Tom agreed, and they stopped dancing to tidy the park. They picked up the trash and put it in the bin.

When they finished, they felt proud of their work. "Now the park is clean and pretty again," said Lily. Tom nodded and said, "It's important to keep our home tidy."

And so, Lily and Tom learned that it's good to have fun, but it's also important to take care of the world around them. They promised to always help keep their park clean, and they danced happily ever after.

Lily was upset and she didn't want to leave the treasure box outside. So, she decided to bury it in the ground so that nobody could find it. She dug a hole and put the treasure box inside. But then, she realized that she had made a mistake. She didn't remember where she had buried the treasure box. She started to cry and her parent came to see what was wrong. Lily told her parent what had happened and they both started to look for the treasure box. After a while, they found it and Lily was very happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to race with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends decided to have a race in the park. They all lined up, ready to go. "On your mark, get set, go!" shouted Lily's friend, Sarah. They all ran as fast as they could, but Lily won the race!

After the race, they all sat down to eat some snacks. Lily's mom had packed some carrots, apples, and pepper slices. Lily didn't like the pepper, so she hid it under her napkin. "Lily, did you eat your pepper?" asked her mom. "No, I don't like it," replied Lily.

Later that day, Lily went to her grandma's house. "What did you do today?" asked her grandma. "I raced with my friends and won!" said Lily. "That's great!" said her grandma. "Did you eat all your snacks?" "Yes, except for the pepper. I hid it under my napkin," said Lily. Her grandma laughed and said, "Maybe next time you'll like it!"

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird liked to fly high in the sky and soar through the clouds. One day, the bird saw a shiny ornament on a tree. The bird thought it was pretty and wanted to take it. 

The bird flew down to the tree and tried to grab the ornament. But the ornament was stuck and wouldn't come off. The bird tried and tried, but it couldn't get the ornament off the tree. 

A squirrel saw the bird struggling and said, "Why are you being so foolish? That ornament is not worth getting stuck for." 

But the bird didn't listen and kept trying. Eventually, the bird got the ornament off the tree, but its wing got stuck in the process. The bird couldn't fly anymore and was stuck on the ground. 

The bird realized too late that the squirrel was right. It was a foolish decision to try and get the ornament. Now, the bird couldn't fly and was stuck on the ground forever.

As they walked, they saw a big tree with a fine-looking branch. Lily wanted to climb up and see if she could spot the treasure from above. Benny warned her that it might be dangerous, but Lily was determined. She started to climb, but as she reached the top, the branch suddenly twisted and broke! Lily fell down and hurt her arm.

Benny felt very sorry for her, and helped her up. "I told you it was dangerous," he said. "But don't worry, we'll find the treasure another way. And remember, it's not always about finding treasure. It's about having fun and staying safe." Lily learned her lesson and they continued their adventure, looking for treasure in a safer way.

Once upon a time, there was an old bear who lived in the forest. He loved to eat honey from the beehive. The bear was very old and could not climb the tree anymore to get the honey. 

One day, a little girl came into the forest to pick berries. The old bear saw her and thought she might be able to help him. He asked her, "Can you get me some honey from the beehive?" The little girl agreed and climbed up the tree to get the honey.

As she reached for the honey, the bees started buzzing around her. She quickly grabbed the honey and ran back down the tree. The old bear was very happy and thanked her. He said, "You have surrendered the honey to me. Thank you, my dear."

From that day on, the little girl would come to the forest often to help the elderly bear get his honey. She learned that surrendering something can make someone else very happy.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making things with blocks, cars, dolls and animals. Lily had a big idea. She wanted to make a green dragon with glue and paper. She asked Ben to help her.

"Ben, do you want to make a green dragon with me?" Lily said.

"Yes, I like dragons. They are big and strong and can fly," Ben said.

They went to the craft table and found some glue, scissors, paper and crayons. They cut out a long body, a tail, a head, wings and spikes. They colored them green with crayons. Then they used glue to stick them together.

"Look, our dragon is almost done. It is very green and scary," Lily said.

"It is the best dragon ever. But it needs something more. It needs eyes and teeth and fire," Ben said.

They looked around for something to make eyes and teeth and fire. They saw a jar of glitter on the shelf. It was shiny and sparkly and had many colors. They thought it would be perfect for their dragon.

"Let's use glitter for the eyes and teeth and fire. It will make our dragon look more real," Ben said.

"Good idea. But we have to be careful. Glitter can be messy and sticky," Lily said.

They took the jar of glitter and opened it. They sprinkled some glitter on the dragon's head, mouth and wings. They made eyes and teeth and fire with glitter. They were very happy with their dragon. It looked very green and shiny and scary.

But they did not notice that some glitter fell on the floor, on the couch, on the table and on their clothes. They also did not notice that the glue was not dry yet. The glitter and the glue mixed together and became very sticky and hard. They stuck to the dragon, to each other and to everything they touched.

"Uh-oh, we have a problem. We are stuck to the dragon and to everything else. We can't move," Ben said.

"Help, help, we need help. Mom, dad, where are you?" Lily said.

They heard their mom and dad coming from the kitchen. They saw the mess in the living room. They saw Lily and Ben and the dragon covered in glitter and glue. They were very surprised and angry.

"What have you done? How did this happen? You are in big trouble," mom said.

"We are sorry, mom. We wanted to make a green dragon with glue and paper. But we used glitter too. And the glitter and the glue became very sticky and hard. And we stuck to everything," Lily said.

"We didn't mean to make a mess. We just wanted to have fun. Can you help us get unstuck?" Ben said.

Mom and dad sighed. They got some scissors, some water and some towels. They carefully cut the glitter and the glue from Lily and Ben and the dragon. They cleaned the floor, the couch, the table and their clothes. They threw away the dragon. They were not happy.

"You should not have used glitter and glue without asking us. You should have been more careful and tidy. You made a big mess and wasted a lot of things. You are not allowed to play with glitter and glue for a long time," dad said.

"We are sorry, dad. We learned our lesson. We will not use glitter and glue again. We will play with something else," Lily and Ben said.

They hugged their mom and dad and said they loved them. They went to their room and played with their toys. They did not make any more dragons. They made something else. Something that did not need glitter and glue. Something that was not green. Something that was not sticky and hard. Something that was more simple and safe. They made a house. A house with blocks. A house with cars. A house with dolls. A house with animals. A house that was fun. A house that was theirs.

"Who did this?" Mom asks. She is angry. She sees Anna and Ben playing with their toys. She shows them the pepper. "Did you bury my pepper?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They are scared. They know they did something bad. They are not lucky anymore. They are sorry.

"We are sorry, Mom. We were playing pirates. We thought it was a treasure. We have a map. We can show you." Anna says.

Mom sighs. She is not happy, but she is not angry anymore. She loves Anna and Ben. She knows they are just kids. She teaches them not to take things that are not theirs. Lily ran to Ben. She hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?"

The car stopped. The driver got out. He was sorry too. He said, "I'm sorry, kid. Are you okay?"

Ben said, "No. I'm not okay. My leg hurts. Why did you hit me?"

The driver said, "I didn't mean to hit you. You didn't yield. You didn't let me go first. You have to follow the signs. They are there to keep you safe."

Ben said, "What is yield?"

Lily said, "Yield means to let other bikes or cars go first. You have to look and wait. It's like saying please."

Ben said, "Oh. I didn't know that. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to be rude. I just wanted to win the race."

Lily said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But next time, please yield. It's more important to be safe than to win."

Ben said, "Okay, Lily. I will. Thank you for being my friend."

Lily said, "You're welcome, Ben. You're my friend too."

The driver said, "You're very brave, kids. And very smart. You learned a new word today. And a new lesson. I'm proud of you. But you should still go to the doctor and check your leg. It might be broken."

Ben said, "Okay, mister. Thank you for being nice."

The driver said, "You're welcome, kid. I'm sorry for being fast."

He called an ambulance. The ambulance came. It took Ben and Lily to the hospital. Their parents came too. They were worried. But they were also happy. They hugged their kids. They thanked the driver. They asked him a lot of questions. He answered them. He was honest. He was sorry. He learned a lesson too. He said he would be more careful. He said he would yield. He said he would say please. He said he would be a better driver. He said he would be a better person. He said he would be a friend.

The cat ran after Ben's bike and tried to catch his tire. Ben did not like that. He shouted at the cat, "Go away, cat! You are not playing. You are bothering me!"

The cat did not reply. It kept running after Ben's tire. It thought it was fun. Lily saw the cat and laughed. She said to Ben, "Don't be mad, Ben. The cat is just curious. It likes your bike."

Ben did not think it was funny. He said to Lily, "No, Lily. The cat is nosy. It does not like my bike. It wants to ruin my bike. It is a bad cat!"

Lily did not agree. She said to Ben, "No, Ben. The cat is not bad. It is just a cat. It does not know better. It is a cute cat!"

Ben and Lily argued about the cat. They forgot about their game. The cat got bored and left. It found another yard with another bike. It ran after that bike's tire. It did not care what Ben and Lily said. It was a nosy cat.

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to play on the farm with the animals. They liked the pigs, the sheep, the horses and the chickens. But they did not like the cow. The cow was ugly. It had a big nose, a long tail and spots all over. The cow also made a loud noise.

One day, Tim and Sam decided to tease the cow. They threw stones at it, pulled its tail and made faces at it. The cow was angry. It frown and moo. It ran after Tim and Sam. Tim and Sam were scared. They tried to run away, but they were too slow. The cow caught them and kicked them with its hoofs. Tim and Sam cried and hurt.

Mom and Dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw Tim and Sam on the ground and the cow standing over them. They were angry and sad. They scold Tim and Sam for being mean to the cow. They took them to the house and put bandages on their wounds. They told them to stay in their room and think about what they did. Tim and Sam were sorry. They wished they had been nice to the cow. But it was too late. The cow did not like them anymore. The cow was ugly, but Tim and Sam were uglier.

Tom and Sue were friends. They liked to play and laugh. One day, they went to a restaurant with their moms. The restaurant had many foods. Tom and Sue wanted to eat pizza and ice cream. Their moms said no. They said pizza and ice cream were not healthy. They said Tom and Sue had to eat salad and soup. Tom and Sue did not like salad and soup. They made faces and said yuck.

The moms said salad and soup were good for them. They said Tom and Sue would grow strong and smart. They said pizza and ice cream would make them sick and tired. They said Tom and Sue had to eat what they gave them. Tom and Sue did not listen. They had a plan. They waited for their moms to look away. Then they switched their plates. Tom gave his salad and soup to Sue. Sue gave her pizza and ice cream to Tom. They smiled and ate what they wanted.

The moms did not notice. They talked and drank. They paid the bill and left. Tom and Sue were happy. They thought they were clever. They did not know what would happen next. They did not know they would suffer.

On the way home, Tom and Sue felt bad. Their tummies hurt. They felt dizzy and hot. They wanted to throw up. They cried and said sorry. Their moms were worried. They took them to the doctor. The doctor said Tom and Sue ate too much pizza and ice cream. He said they had a tummy ache. He gave them some medicine and told them to rest. He said they should eat healthy foods next time. He said they should listen to their moms.

Tom and Sue learned their lesson. They said they would never switch their plates again. They said they would eat salad and soup. They said they would be good. Their moms hugged them and said they loved them. They said they were glad they were okay. They said they hoped they would feel better soon. Tom and Sue said they hoped so too. They said they were sorry for making their moms worry. They said they were sorry for suffering.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were brave knights and princesses. They had a big stick for a sword and a shiny crown for a king.

"Look, I am the king of the park!" Ben said, putting the crown on his head. "You have to do what I say!"

"No, I don't!" Lily said, grabbing the stick. "I am a knight and I will fight you!"

They laughed and chased each other around the swings and the slide. They did not see the big dog that was watching them from behind a bush. The dog was hungry and angry. It had a scary face and sharp teeth.

The dog decided to attack. It ran out of the bush and barked loudly. Ben and Lily were scared. They dropped the stick and the crown and ran away. The dog followed them, snapping at their heels.

"Help, help!" Ben and Lily cried. "There is a scary dog!"

A man heard their cries and came to help. He was the owner of the dog. He grabbed the dog by the collar and shook it.

"Bad dog, bad dog!" he said. "You are not supposed to chase children!"

He apologized to Ben and Lily and took the dog away. Ben and Lily were relieved. They hugged each other and picked up their stick and crown.

"Thank you, mister!" they said.

"You're welcome, kids," the man said. "Be careful next time. Not all dogs are friendly."

Ben and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They decided to play something else. They did not want to be the king and the knight anymore. They wanted to be the dog and the cat. They thought that would be more fun.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big pond with many ducks. Tom likes ducks. He runs to the pond and tries to catch one. Mia follows him.

"Tom, be careful!" Mia says. "Ducks do not like to be caught. They will bite you!"

But Tom does not listen. He grabs a duck by the wing. The duck is heavy and angry. It quacks loudly and pecks Tom's hand. Tom lets go of the duck and cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom says. "The duck hurt me!"

Mia runs to Tom and hugs him. She squeezes him gently and says, "I'm sorry, Tom. The duck was scared. You should not catch ducks. You should feed them bread."

Tom nods and wipes his tears. He says, "I'm sorry, duck. I will not catch you again. I will feed you bread."

Mia smiles and says, "That's good, Tom. Come on, let's go find some bread. Maybe the duck will forgive you."

They walk to the bench where their mom is sitting. She has a bag of bread. She gives them some pieces and says, "What happened, kids? Why are you crying, Tom?"

Tom and Mia tell her what happened. She says, "Oh, Tom, you should be more gentle with animals. They have feelings too. But I'm glad you learned your lesson. Here, take some bread and feed the ducks. They will like that."

Tom and Mia say, "Thank you, mom." They go back to the pond and throw some bread to the ducks. The ducks come closer and eat the bread. They quack happily. Tom and Mia smile and watch them. They feel happy too.

Ben and Tom were brothers who liked to fish. They had a big rod that their dad gave them. It was a mighty rod that could catch many fish. One day, they went to the lake with their rod and some worms.

They threw the worms in the water and waited for the fish to bite. Ben saw a big splash and felt a tug on his rod. He smiled and said, "I got one, Tom! I got one!"

Tom smiled too and helped Ben pull the rod. But the fish was too strong and too fast. It pulled the rod out of Ben's hands and dragged it into the water. Ben and Tom watched in shock as their mighty rod disappeared.

They ran to their dad and told him what happened. Their dad was not angry. He hugged them and said, "Don't worry, boys. It's just a rod. You can always get another one. But you can't get another fish like that. You just met the biggest fish in the lake. Maybe he will come back someday and give you your rod back. He might even smile at you."

Ben and Tom felt better and laughed. They decided to call the fish Roddy. They hoped to see him again and maybe catch him with a new rod. They knew he was a mighty fish, but they were mighty brothers too.

But the dog did not go away. It smelled them and found them. It jumped on them and bit them. Tim and Lily screamed and cried. They were hurt and bleeding. They wished someone would help them.

But no one came. The park was empty. No one heard them or saw them. They were alone and in pain. They were very unlucky.

The dog left them and ran away. Tim and Lily lay on the ground. They were too weak to move. They looked at each other and said sorry. They said they loved each other. They closed their eyes and stopped breathing.

The moral of the story is: Be careful of strangers and dangerous animals. Always stay close to your parents or guardians. Don't go to places where you are not safe. Worry can save your life.

"What are you doing here?" she asked. "This elevator is broken. It needs to be fixed. You could have been hurt. Who pressed all these buttons?"

Ben and Mia pointed at each other. They did not want to get in trouble. The man sighed and shook his head.

"They did it," he said. "They were playing with the elevator and did not let me use it. They were very persistent and annoying."

The woman looked at Ben and Mia. She saw that they were scared and sorry. She decided to teach them a lesson.

She told them that the elevator was not a toy, but a machine that helped people move around the building. She told them that they should be kind and respectful to other people who needed the elevator.

Ben and Mia listened and learned. They felt ashamed and apologized to the man and the woman. They promised to never play with the elevator again. They asked the woman to take them back to their floor.

Ben and Mia agreed and smiled. They decided to play with their blocks and make a tower. They did not want to play with the elevator anymore. They learned their lesson. They were good twins.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who wanted to read a book but no matter what he tried he couldn't fit his arm behind the book to pull it off the shelf. 

The boy started to get frustrated. He yelled at the book, "Come down! You're bad!"

Just then, his mom walked in the room. She saw what was happening and said,
"It may be true that the book won't come down, but calling it bad isn't nice. Let's look for another solution."

The boy thought for a minute and then said, "Maybe if I pushed it from the top it would move."

His mom smiled and said, "Let's try that!"

Sure enough, pushing the book from the top was just the right solution and the boy was able to take the book off the shelf.

The moral of this story is that there is often more than one solution to a problem. Even when it may seem that there is no way the problem can be solved, if you think creatively you may find just the right solution!

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Sarah. Sarah was three years old and she lived with her mum and dad. Her mum was always very gentle and kind.

"Oh, Sarah," her mum said kindly, putting her arm around Sarah's shoulder. "What's the matter?"

"The butterfly flew away," Sarah sniffed.

Her mum smiled warmly. "Don't worry, Sarah. You can't always trust the way things seem. Now, why don't you come inside for some tea?"

Sarah trusted her mum and followed her inside for a cup of tea. The tea was warm and comforting - Sarah felt much better afterwards. 

Even though Sarah was only three years old, she knew that her mum was always gentle and kind, and always had her best interests at heart. 

From that day on, Sarah never lost sight of how delicate things can be - and she trusted her mum with all of her heart.

Tim was scared. The box shook more and more. Suddenly, the box fell apart. Tim was sad because his fun time was over. The unusual cardboard box was broken, and he couldn't play with it anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog. The frog lived in a small pond. The frog had a best friend, a yellow duck. They liked to play together.

One day, the green frog found a big box. The box was closed. The frog said, "Duck, let's open the box." The duck said, "Yes, let's do it!"

They found scissors to open the box. The frog cut the wrap with the scissors. Inside the box, they found a big red ball. The green frog and the yellow duck played with the red ball all day long. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim did not like to eat broccoli. One day, his mom made a big plate of broccoli for dinner. Tim looked at the broccoli and said, "I don't want to eat that!"

His mom said, "But Tim, broccoli is harmless and good for you. It will make you big and strong. Please try it." Tim shook his head and did not eat the broccoli.

The next day, Tim saw his friend Jack. Jack was very strong and could lift heavy things. Tim asked Jack, "How did you get so strong?" Jack said, "I eat my broccoli every day!" Tim thought about it and decided to try eating broccoli too.

That night, Tim ate all his broccoli. He ate broccoli every day after that. Soon, Tim became big and strong like Jack. Tim learned that if he repeats something good, like eating broccoli, it can help him grow and be strong.

One day, a warm sun was up in the sky. A little girl named Amy went to the garden. She saw a big onion in the dirt. She wanted to pick it up and show her mom.

Amy tried to pull the onion, but it was stuck. She twisted and twisted, but it would not come out. A little red bird saw her and flew down. "Why are you sad?" the bird asked.

"I want to show this onion to my mom, but I can't get it out," Amy said. The bird had an idea. "Twist and pull at the same time!" Amy did what the bird said. The onion came out of the dirt. Amy was happy and thanked the bird. She ran to show her mom the big onion.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a toy iron that she loved to play with. Mia would pretend to iron her doll's clothes every day. One day, Mia could not find her toy iron. It was hidden somewhere in her room.

Mia looked and looked for her hidden toy iron. She felt sad and did not know what to do. She asked her big brother, Tom, for help. Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's squeeze all your toys and maybe we will find the iron."

Mia and Tom started to squeeze all the toys in the room. They squeezed the teddy bear, the ball, and even the toy car. Finally, Mia squeezed her toy box and heard a sound. She opened the box and found her hidden toy iron! Mia was so happy, and she thanked Tom for his help. From that day on, Mia always put her toy iron back in the toy box, so it would never be hidden again.

"Ben, your dragon is broken!" Lily said. "It doesn't fire!"

Ben frowned. He pressed the stick himself. He heard a hiss and saw a puff of smoke. But the smoke was not from the dragon. It was from behind a bush.

"What happened here?" she asked. "How did you start this fire?"

"Beep beep! Move out of the way!" Ben shouted as he zoomed his car past Lily's bike.

"Hey, that's not nice!" Lily said. "You almost hit me!"

"Sorry, I was just having fun," Ben replied. "Do you want to race with me?"

Lily nodded. She liked to race with Ben. They lined up their vehicles at the start line and counted to three.

"One, two, three, go!" they said together and pushed their vehicles forward.

Lily's bike was faster than Ben's car. She reached the finish line first and cheered.

"I won, I won!" she said happily.

Ben was sad. He wanted to win too. He looked at his car and saw that one of the wheels was loose.

"That's not fair!" he said. "My car is broken!"

He threw his car on the ground and stomped his feet.

Lily saw that Ben was angry. She felt sorry for him. She picked up his car and fixed the wheel.

"Here, Ben," she said. "Your car is fine now. Do you want to try again?"

Ben looked at Lily. She was smiling and holding his car. He felt ashamed. He had been rude to her and she had been kind to him.

"Thank you, Lily," he said. "You are a good friend. I'm sorry I was mean to you."

He took his car and hugged Lily.

"It's okay, Ben," she said. "We all make mistakes. The important thing is to say sorry and be nice."

They hugged and smiled. They decided to play together again, but this time they shared their vehicles and took turns.

They had more fun that way.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to your friends and share your toys.

Lily and her mom went to the grocery store to buy some food. Lily liked to help her mom push the cart and look at the things on the shelves. She saw some apples, some cheese, some bread, and some cookies. She wanted to eat the cookies, but her mom said they had to pay first.

When they got to the cashier, Lily saw a big truck outside the window. It was yellow and shiny, and it had a loud horn. Lily pointed at the truck and said, "Look, mom, a truck!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, that's a truck. It's a delivery truck. It brings food to the grocery store."

Lily watched the truck as it backed up to the door. She heard a beep-beep-beep sound as the truck reversed. She thought it was funny how the truck moved backwards. She said, "Mom, why does the truck reverse?"

Her mom explained, "The truck reverses to get closer to the door. Then the driver can unload the food and put it in the store. It's easier than driving forward and turning around."

Lily nodded. She understood. She said, "Can I reverse too?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Sure, you can reverse. But be careful not to bump into anyone or anything."

Lily giggled and said, "OK, mom." She let go of the cart and walked backwards. She said, "Beep-beep-beep, I'm a truck!"

She reversed until she reached the end of the aisle. Then she turned around and saw a pale boy with a red nose and a hat. He looked sick and sad. He was holding a box of tissues. Lily felt sorry for him. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?"

The boy sniffled and said, "I'm Ben. I have a cold."

Lily said, "Oh, I'm sorry. Do you want a cookie? I have some in the cart."

Ben smiled and said, "Yes, please. Thank you."

Lily ran back to the cart and grabbed a cookie. She gave it to Ben and said, "Here you go. I hope you feel better soon."

Ben took the cookie and said, "Thank you, Lily. You're very nice."

Lily and Ben became friends. They shared the cookie and talked about trucks and toys. Lily's mom paid for the food and said, "Lily, it's time to go. Say goodbye to your new friend."

Lily hugged Ben and said, "Bye, Ben. I hope you get well soon. Maybe we can play again sometime."

Ben hugged Lily and said, "Bye, Lily. Thank you for the cookie and the hug. You made me happy."

Lily and her mom left the grocery store. Lily waved at the truck and said, "Beep-beep-beep, bye-bye, truck!"

The end.

"Are the fireworks broken?" Ben asked, looking out the window.

Sara and Ben nodded, but they felt sad and disappointed. They liked fireworks, but they didn't like the gray smoke and the loud boom. They wished they could see the fireworks as they had imagined them.

Later, when they were leaving the park, they saw the man again. This time, he took Lily away and nobody could find her. Her mommy was very sad and cried a lot. They never saw Lily again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly and sing in the spring. One day, Tweety flew too high and got dizzy. Tweety started to fly in circles and almost fell out of the sky.

A wise old owl saw Tweety and asked, "What happened?" Tweety replied, "I flew too high and got dizzy." The owl said, "It's not good to lie to yourself. You flew too high because you wanted to show off."

Tweety felt ashamed and said, "I'm sorry, you're right. I just wanted to show off." The owl replied, "It's okay to be proud of yourself, but never lie about it. Always be honest with yourself and others."

From that day on, Tweety learned to be honest and never flew too high again. And the wise old owl and Tweety became good friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to fish with his dad. They would go to the lake every weekend and catch lots of fish. Timmy's dad had a special rod that he would use to catch the biggest fish.

One day, Timmy saw an empty bucket on the shore and asked his dad if they could catch enough fish to fill it up. His dad said, "Sure, let's act fast and catch as many as we can."

They started fishing and caught lots of fish, but they kept throwing them back because they weren't big enough. Timmy wanted to keep some of the smaller ones, but his dad said they needed to let them grow bigger.

Suddenly, Timmy's dad felt a big tug on his rod. He knew it was a huge fish and started reeling it in. But the fish was too strong and the rod snapped in half! They lost the fish and all the others they caught were too small to fill the empty bucket.

Timmy's dad explained to him that sometimes we need to be patient and wait for the right moment. We can't always act quickly and expect everything to work out. The moral of the story is that patience is important and rushing can lead to bad outcomes.

The ball wanted to help the small human. So, it started to roll around the park, looking for the important toy. As it rolled, it saw something shiny under a bush. The ball rolled closer and saw that it was the important toy!

The ball rolled back to the small human with the toy. The small human was so happy! "Thank you, ball," said the small human. "You found my important toy!" From that day on, the ball and the small human became best friends, and they played together in the park every day.

One day, a little adorable cat named Fluffy went for a walk. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. Fluffy jumped and climbed up the tree. She saw many things from up high. She saw a bird, a dog, and a big house.

Fluffy saw a cobweb on a branch. A small spider lived in the cobweb. Fluffy said, "Hi, spider! I like your cobweb." The spider said, "Thank you, Fluffy. I worked hard to make it."

Fluffy wanted to play with the spider, but she was scared. The spider said, "Don't be scared, Fluffy. I won't hurt you." Fluffy decided to surrender her fear and play with the spider. They played together and became good friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a wise old dog named Max. Max loved to help people find things they had lost. He had a very good nose for it.

One day, there was a big earthquake. The ground shook and everyone was scared. Max knew he had to help. He went outside and saw a little girl named Lily. She was crying because she lost her toy bunny during the earthquake.

Max said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will help you find your toy bunny." Max sniffed the ground and started to look for the bunny. Lily followed Max as he searched.

After a while, Max found the toy bunny under a big tree. Lily was so happy and hugged Max. She said, "Thank you, Max. You are the wisest dog ever!"

From that day on, Max and Lily became best friends. They played together every day, and everyone in the town knew that Max was the wisest dog who could find anything.

Together, they sat under the tree and shared the delicious apple. They laughed and talked about their success. From that day on, Amy and Tom always helped each other and shared their yummy treats. They were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel named Tim. Tim loved to cook acorns. One day, while he was cooking, he saw his friend, the bird named Sam.

"Hi Sam," said Tim. "Do you want to try my acorn?"

"Sure," said Sam. "I have never eaten an acorn before."

Sam took a bite of the acorn, but it was too hard. "Ouch!" said Sam. "This acorn hurt my beak!"

"I am sorry," said Tim. "I will cook the acorn more so it is not hard."

Tim cooked the acorn more, and then Sam tried it again. This time, it was not hard and did not hurt Sam's beak. They both laughed and ate the acorns together. They were very happy and had a fun day.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play together at the park. One day, they see a big bus on the street. The bus is yellow and loud.

"Wow, look at the bus!" Sam says. "It is so big and yellow. I want to ride on the bus."

Lily says, "No, Sam. The bus is not for us. The bus is for big kids and grown-ups. We are too small for the bus. We have to walk to the park."

Sam does not like what Lily says. He thinks Lily is bossy. He says, "You are not the boss of me, Lily. I can do what I want. I want to ride on the bus. I will go and ask the bus driver."

Lily says, "Sam, wait! The bus is not safe for us. The bus driver will not let you on. The bus will go too fast and too far. You will get lost and scared. Please, Sam, stay with me."

But Sam does not listen to Lily. He runs to the bus and tries to get on. The bus driver sees Sam and says, "Hey, little boy, what are you doing? You cannot ride on the bus. You need a ticket and a grown-up. Go back to your friend."

Sam feels sad and silly. He says, "Sorry, bus driver. I just wanted to ride on the bus. It looked fun."

The bus driver says, "It's okay, little boy. Maybe when you are bigger, you can ride on the bus. But for now, you have to stay with your friend. She cares about you and wants you to be safe. Go and say sorry to her."

Sam goes back to Lily and says, "Sorry, Lily. You were right. The bus is not for us. You are not bossy. You are a good friend. Can we still play at the park?"

Lily says, "Of course, Sam. I am glad you are back. I was worried about you. Come on, let's go and play at the park."

They hold hands and walk to the park. They see a swing and a slide and a sandbox. They have fun and forget about the bus. They are happy.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were spies and look for clues. Lily had a magnifying glass and Tom had a walkie-talkie.

"Tom, Tom, do you copy?" Lily said into the walkie-talkie. "I found something."

"What is it, Lily?" Tom said.

"Come and see. It's a big hole in the fence. Maybe someone made it to sneak in."

Lily and Tom ran to the hole. They saw a big dog on the other side. The dog was barking and growling. It looked angry and scary.

"Oh no, it's a threat!" Lily said. "We have to prepare."

"How do we prepare, Lily?" Tom said.

"We have to find something to scare the dog away. Maybe a stick or a stone."

Lily and Tom looked around for something to use. They found a big branch and a shiny can. They held them in their hands and walked slowly to the hole.

"Go away, dog!" Lily shouted. "We are spies and we have weapons!"

She waved the branch and threw the can. The can made a loud noise when it hit the ground. The dog was surprised and ran away.

"Yay, we did it!" Tom said. "We are good spies!"

Lily and Tom high-fived and hugged. They were happy and proud. They went back to their house and told their mom what they did. She gave them cookies and milk and said they were brave and clever.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys on the couch. They liked to pretend they were pirates and princesses. Tom had a sword and Lily had a crown.

"Arrr, I am the captain of this ship!" Tom said. "You have to do what I say, princess!"

"No, I don't!" Lily said. "I am the queen of this castle! You have to be nice to me, pirate!"

They started to argue and push each other. They did not see that their mom was watching them.

"Tom, Lily, stop fighting!" their mom said. "You are making a mess of the couch and the pillows. You have to share and play nicely, or you will have to go to your rooms."

Tom and Lily looked at their mom. They did not want to go to their rooms. They wanted to keep playing.

"Sorry, mom," they said.

"Promise me you will be good and clean up the couch when you are done," their mom said.

"Promise, mom," they said.

They hugged their mom and gave her a kiss. Then they went back to playing. They decided to be friends and not fight. They had fun pretending to sail the seas and rule the land. They remembered their promise and put the toys and the pillows back where they belonged. The couch was hard, but they did not mind. They were happy.

Anna and Ben were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. But sometimes they fought over the blocks. Anna wanted the red blocks and Ben wanted the blue blocks. They did not want to share.

"Give me that block!" Anna said. She reached for a blue block that Ben had.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. He pulled the block away from Anna.

Anna was angry. She slapped Ben on the arm. Ben cried out. He slapped Anna back on the cheek. Anna cried too.

Their mom heard the noise. She came into the room. She saw the blocks and the tears and the red marks.

"What happened here?" she asked.

"Anna slapped me!" Ben said.

"Ben slapped me!" Anna said.

Mom was not happy. She picked up both of them and sat them on the couch.

"You should not slap each other. That hurts. And it's not nice. You need to say sorry and hug each other. And then you need to play nicely and share the blocks. Do you understand?" she said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They felt sorry. They said sorry and hugged each other. Mom smiled and kissed them.

"Good. Now you can go back to play. But remember, no more slapping. OK?" she said.

Anna and Ben said OK. They went back to the blocks. They decided to build a big tower together. They used the red blocks and the blue blocks. They were happy. They had a victory. They had a big, chubby tower. And they had each other.

Lily liked to play with her case of toys. She had dolls, cars, blocks and animals in her case. She would take them out and make stories with them. She would talk to them and hug them and pretend they were her friends.

One day, Lily wanted to play with her case of toys, but she could not find it. She looked in her room, in the living room, in the kitchen, but it was not there. She asked her mom and dad, but they did not know where it was. Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted her case of toys back.

She decided to look in the garden. Maybe she left it there when she played outside. She put on her shoes and coat and went out. She saw a big pile of leaves. She thought maybe her case of toys was under the leaves. She ran to the pile and started to dig. She hoped to find her case of toys.

But she did not find her case of toys. She found something else. She found a big, round, orange pumpkin. It had a face carved on it. It had a stem on top. It had a light inside. It was a jack-o-lantern. Lily was surprised. She did not know who put it there. She thought it was funny and scary.

She picked up the jack-o-lantern and looked at it. She saw a hole on the bottom. She wondered what was inside. She put her hand in the hole and felt something soft and wet. It was the pumpkin seeds and pulp. It smelled sweet and tasty. Lily took out some seeds and pulp and tasted them. She liked them. She thought they were yummy.

She ate more and more seeds and pulp. She did not notice that the jack-o-lantern was getting smaller and smaller. She did not notice that the light was getting dimmer and dimmer. She did not notice that the face was getting fainter and fainter. She ate until there was nothing left. She ate the whole jack-o-lantern.

She looked at her hand and saw only a stem. She looked at the ground and saw only leaves. She looked around and saw no jack-o-lantern. She realized what she had done. She had made the jack-o-lantern vanish. She felt happy and proud. She had eaten a whole pumpkin. She had solved the mystery of the missing case of toys. She had found a tasty treat. She smiled and laughed. She ran back to the house to tell her mom and dad. She hoped they would not be mad. She hoped they would be proud. She hoped they would have more pumpkins.

Tom and Mia liked to play with cardboard boxes. They made houses, cars, and castles with them. One day, they found a big cardboard box in the garage. They decided to make a spaceship with it.

They cut out windows and doors with scissors. They drew buttons and stars with crayons. They put a blanket inside to make it cozy. They were very proud of their spaceship.

"Let's go to the moon!" Tom said.

"OK, but we need a rocket," Mia said.

She looked around and saw a lighter on a shelf. She did not know what it was, but it looked shiny and fun. She took it and brought it to the spaceship.

"Look, Tom, I found a rocket!" she said.

She pressed the lighter and a flame came out. She was amazed and scared. She dropped the lighter on the cardboard.

"Uh-oh," Tom said.

The cardboard caught fire. It burned very fast and very hot. Tom and Mia screamed and ran out of the garage. They saw their mom and dad coming. They were angry and worried.

"What did you do?" their mom asked.

"We made a spaceship," Tom said.

"And a rocket," Mia said.

They pointed to the garage. It was full of smoke and flames. Their mom and dad called the firemen. They scolded Tom and Mia. They said they were very naughty and dangerous. They said they could have hurt themselves and the house.

Tom and Mia felt very embarrassed and sorry. They cried and hugged their mom and dad. They said they were sorry and they would never play with fire again. But their mom and dad said they were grounded for a long time. They said they had to throw away all their cardboard boxes. They said they had to learn a lesson.

Tom and Mia were very sad. They lost their spaceship and their fun. They wished they had never found the lighter. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They wished they had a better ending.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big box full of dolls, cars, animals and blocks. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a zip that looked like a magic wand. It had a button and a light on it.

"What is this?" Lily asked, picking up the zip.

"I don't know. Maybe it's a magic zip. Let's try it!" Ben said, grabbing the zip from Lily.

He pointed the zip at a doll and pressed the button. The light flashed and the doll shrank to the size of a peanut.

"Wow! It is a magic zip! It can make things small!" Ben said, laughing.

"That's not funny! That's my doll! Give it back!" Lily said, angry.

She tried to take the zip from Ben, but he ran away. He pointed the zip at more toys and made them shrink. Lily chased him, but he was too fast. He shrank the cars, the animals and the blocks. He even shrank Lily's teddy bear.

"Stop it! Stop it! You're ruining our toys!" Lily shouted, crying.

Ben was having too much fun. He didn't listen to Lily. He pointed the zip at her and pressed the button. The light flashed and Lily shrank to the size of a mouse.

"Ha ha! Now you're small too!" Ben said, holding the zip.

But then he heard a loud roar. He turned around and saw a big cat. The cat had seen the small Lily and wanted to catch her. The cat ran towards Lily, who was scared.

"Help! Help! Ben, help me!" Lily screamed.

Ben realized he had made a big mistake. He had shrank his sister and put her in danger. He felt sorry and scared. He wanted to make her big again, but he didn't know how. He looked at the zip, but it didn't have a button to make things big. It only had a button to make things small.

He had to think fast. He pointed the zip at the cat and pressed the button. The light flashed and the cat shrank to the size of a bug.

"Phew! That was close!" Ben said, relieved.

He picked up the small Lily and hugged her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry I shrank your toys and you. I was being silly and mean. I won't do it again. I love you, Lily." Ben said, sorry.

"I love you too, Ben. But how are we going to make everything big again?" Lily asked, worried.

"I don't know. Maybe we can find a magic zip that can make things big. Or maybe we can ask Mom or Dad for help. Or maybe we can wait until the magic wears off. I hope it does." Ben said, hopeful.

They put the small toys and the small cat in the box and carried it to their room. They hoped they could find a way to fix their problem. They learned a lesson. They learned that magic zips can be fun, but also dangerous. They learned to be careful and kind with their toys and each other.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big kangaroo near the fence. They wanted to pet it and feed it some grass.

"Let's go and say hello to the kangaroo," Tom said.

"OK, but be careful. It might hop away or kick us," Lily said.

They ran to the fence and reached out their hands. The kangaroo looked at them and sniffed their fingers. It seemed friendly and curious.

But then, a loud noise scared the kangaroo. It was a car horn from the road. The kangaroo jumped back and ran to the other side of the park. Tom and Lily followed it, hoping to catch up.

They did not see the sign that said "Do not enter. Kangaroo enclosure. Lock the gate behind you." They opened the gate and ran inside. They did not lock the gate.

The kangaroo was hiding behind a tree. Tom and Lily tried to coax it out with some more grass. They did not notice another kangaroo behind them. It was bigger and stronger than the first one. It did not like strangers in its home.

It growled and charged at Tom and Lily. They screamed and ran back to the gate. But the gate was closed. Someone had locked it from the outside. They were trapped with the angry kangaroo.

"Help! Help! Let us out!" Tom and Lily shouted.

They banged on the gate and cried. They felt very weak and scared.

Luckily, a park ranger heard their cries. He came to the gate and saw what had happened. He unlocked the gate and let Tom and Lily out. He scolded them for entering the kangaroo enclosure without permission. He told them it was very dangerous and they could have been hurt.

Tom and Lily apologized and promised to never do it again. They hugged the park ranger and thanked him for saving them. They learned their lesson and never bothered the kangaroos again.

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys. Tom has a car and Mia has a doll. Mia likes to dress up her doll with different clothes and accessories. She has a box full of them.

"Look, Tom, I have a bandage for my doll. She hurt her leg when she fell from the bed. Do you have a bandage for your car?" Mia asks.

Tom shakes his head. "No, I don't have a bandage for my car. Cars don't need bandages. They need gas and oil and tires."

"But my doll needs a bandage. She is in pain. Can you give me one of your stickers? Maybe I can use it as a bandage." Mia says.

Tom thinks for a moment. He likes his stickers. He has many of them, with different shapes and colors. He looks at Mia's doll. She has a pink dress and a purple hat. He finds a sticker that matches her dress. It is a heart.

"Here, Mia, you can have this sticker. It is a heart. It matches your doll's dress. Maybe it will make her feel better." Tom says.

Mia smiles. She takes the sticker and puts it on her doll's leg. She thinks it looks very pretty. She hugs her doll and thanks Tom.

"Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. You gave me a very unusual bandage. It is a heart. I like it. Do you want to play with my doll and your car? Maybe they can be friends." Mia says.

Tom nods. He likes Mia. He thinks she is very creative. He picks up his car and drives it near Mia's doll. He pretends they are talking.

"Hello, doll. I am a car. I like to go fast and make noises. What do you like to do?" Tom says.

"Hello, car. I am a doll. I like to dress up and have tea parties. What is that on your window?" Mia says.

"It is a sticker. It is a star. It matches my car. It is very shiny. Tom gave it to me. He is my friend. What is that on your leg?" Tom says.

"It is a sticker. It is a heart. It matches my dress. It is very pretty. Mia gave it to me. She is my friend. It is a bandage. I hurt my leg. But now I feel better." Mia says.

The car and the doll smile at each other. They think they have a lot in common. They decide to play together. Tom and Mia watch them. They are happy. They think they have very unusual toys. But they love them.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play war with sticks and stones. They pretend to be soldiers and fight the bad guys. One day, they find a big hill near the park. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

"Come on, Sam, follow me!" Tom says. He runs up the hill with his stick. Sam follows him with his stone. They are happy and excited.

But when they reach the top of the hill, they see a big road with many cars and trucks. The cars and trucks make a lot of noise. They honk and beep and roar. Tom and Sam are scared. They cover their ears with their hands.

"Tom, this is too loud! I don't like it!" Sam says. He tries to shout, but Tom can't hear him. Tom is deaf. He can't hear anything. He only sees Sam's mouth moving.

"Sam, what are you saying? I can't hear you!" Tom says. He tries to sign, but Sam can't see him. Sam is looking at the road. He is afraid of the cars and trucks.

Tom and Sam are sad. They can't talk to each other. They can't play war anymore. They want to go back to the park. They hold hands and walk down the hill. They hope to find a quiet place where they can be friends again.

Lily and Max like to play on the lawn. They have a ball and a hoop. They take turns to throw the ball in the hoop. Lily is good at throwing. Max is good at catching.

One day, they have a game. They want to see who can win. They count how many times they can throw the ball in the hoop. Lily throws first. She gets one, two, three. Max claps for her. Then Max throws. He gets one, two, four. He misses the third one. Lily claps for him.

They keep playing. They have fun. They laugh and run. The sun is bright. The grass is green. The ball is red. The hoop is blue.

But then, a dog comes. The dog is big and brown. The dog is crazy. The dog sees the ball. The dog wants the ball. The dog runs to the ball. The dog grabs the ball. The dog runs away with the ball.

Lily and Max are sad. They lose their ball. They can't play anymore. They can't win. They look at the dog. The dog is happy. The dog thinks he wins. The dog plays with the ball on the other lawn. Lily and Max shake their heads. They go inside. They find another toy. They hope the dog will bring back their ball.

Lily was curious about the big pot on the stove. She wanted to see what was inside. She climbed on a chair and reached for the lid. But the lid was hot and heavy. She dropped it on the floor with a loud bang.

"Ouch!" she cried. "What are you doing, Lily?" her mom asked, running into the kitchen. She saw the lid on the floor and the steam coming out of the pot. She was angry and worried. "That's soup, Lily. It's very hot. You could get hurt. You should never touch the stove or the pot. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded, feeling sorry. She did not mean to make her mom angry or to make a mess. She just wanted to see the soup. She liked soup. It smelled good. She wondered what kind of soup it was. Was it chicken soup? Or tomato soup? Or carrot soup?

Her mom picked up the lid and put it back on the pot. She checked the soup and stirred it with a spoon. She smiled at Lily and said, "I'm sorry I yelled at you, Lily. I know you were curious. But you have to be careful in the kitchen. There are many things that can hurt you. Do you want to help me make some bread for the soup?"

Lily smiled back and said, "Yes, please. I like bread. And soup. What kind of soup is it, mom?"

Her mom winked at her and said, "It's a surprise, Lily. You'll find out soon. But first, let's cover our hands with flour and knead the dough. That's fun, right?"

Lily nodded and jumped off the chair. She followed her mom to the table, where a big bowl of dough was waiting. She covered her hands with flour and started to knead the dough. She felt happy and excited. She forgot about the hot lid and the loud bang. She was looking forward to the soup and the bread. She hoped the soup was her favorite kind. She was still curious.

Sara and Tom are friends who like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide that looks fun. Sara wants to go on the slide, but Tom is scared. He thinks the slide is too high and he might fall.

Sara says, "Don't be scared, Tom. The slide is not too high. It is fun. You can go with me. I will hold your hand." Tom says, "No, Sara. I don't want to go on the slide. I want to play on the swings. The swings are not scary. They are gentle."

Sara and Tom discuss what to do. They both want to play, but they like different things. Sara thinks Tom is silly for being scared. Tom thinks Sara is rude for not listening. They start to argue and get angry.

Then, they see a boy who is crying. He has a scratch on his knee. He says he fell from the slide and it hurt. Sara and Tom feel sorry for him. They stop arguing and go to help him. They give him a band-aid and a hug. They ask him if he wants to play with them.

The boy says yes. He says he likes the swings and the slide. He says he can show Tom how to go on the slide safely and he can learn from Sara how to swing high. Sara and Tom agree. They decide to try both things and have fun together.

They learn that it is good to discuss and listen to each other. They learn that it is okay to have different likes and fears. They learn that it is better to be kind and help others than to be angry and fight. They are happy and tired after playing. They go home with their new friend.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and listen to the radio. The radio plays songs and stories and jokes. Lily and Tom laugh at the jokes.

One day, the radio is weak. It makes noises and stops. Lily and Tom are sad. They want to hear the jokes. Tom has an idea. He says, "I can tell jokes. Do you want to hear?"

Lily says, "Yes, please. Tell me a joke."

Tom thinks harder. He says, "What do you call a fish with no eyes?"

Lily says, "I don't know. What?"

Tim and Lily are twins, but they are very different. Tim likes to play with cars and trucks, and Lily likes to play with dolls and dresses. One day, they are in their room, and they see a big carpet on the floor. It is red and soft, and it has many shapes on it.

"Wow, look at this carpet!" Tim says. "It is like a road. I can drive my cars on it."

"No, it is like a garden. I can have a tea party with my dolls on it," Lily says.

They both want to play on the carpet, but they do not want to share. They start to argue and push each other.

"Go away, Lily! This is my carpet!" Tim shouts.

"Stop it, Tim! This is my carpet!" Lily shouts.

They are so angry and loud that they do not hear their mom calling them for lunch. They do not see their dog, Spot, coming into the room. Spot is hungry and curious. He sees the carpet and thinks it is a big toy. He runs to the carpet and starts to bite and pull it.

"Hey, stop that, Spot!" Tim and Lily say. They try to stop him, but he is too strong and fast. He tears the carpet into pieces and makes a big mess.

Mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees the carpet and the twins and the dog. She is very mad and sad.

"What have you done?" she says. "This was a special carpet. It was a gift from your grandma. She made it with love and care. How could you be so selfish and careless?"

Tim and Lily feel bad. They look at the carpet and the mom and the dog. They wish they had been nice and shared. They say they are sorry, but it is too late. The carpet is ruined, and mom is disappointed. They have to go to their beds without lunch. They do not want to play anymore. They have learned a hard lesson.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They saw a furry cat under a tree. The cat was black and white and had a long tail.

"Look, a kitty!" Sara said. "Can we pet it?"

Ben nodded. They walked slowly to the cat. The cat looked at them and meowed. Sara reached out her hand to touch the cat's head. But the cat did not like it. It hissed and scratched Sara's hand with its claws.

"Ow!" Sara cried. "It hurts!" She pulled back her hand and saw blood. She ran to her mom, who was sitting on a bench. Ben followed her.

Mom saw Sara's hand and took out a tissue. She wiped the blood and put a band-aid on it. She hugged Sara and said, "It's okay, honey. The cat was scared. It did not mean to hurt you."

Ben felt sorry for Sara. He wanted to make her feel better. He looked around and saw a rod on the ground. It was a fishing rod that someone had left behind. Ben picked it up and ran to Sara.

"Look, Sara, I found a rod!" Ben said. "We can pretend to fish. Maybe we can catch a big fish and share it with the cat. Then the cat will be happy and not scratch us."

Sara smiled. She liked Ben's idea. She took the rod from Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. Let's go fish."

They ran to the pond and pretended to fish. They had fun and forgot about the cat. They did not catch any fish, but they caught each other's laughter.

Sam and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. They had a big bucket full of worms and beetles. They were very happy.

"Look, Sam, I found a shiny stone!" Mia said, holding up a red pebble.

"Wow, that's pretty! Can I see?" Sam asked, reaching for the pebble.

But before Mia could give it to him, they heard a loud hiss. They looked down and saw a snake. It was black and yellow, and it had a big mouth. It was angry. It wanted the pebble.

"Snake!" Sam and Mia screamed. They dropped the bucket and ran away. They were very scared.

They ran to the house, where their mom was. They told her about the snake. She hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. I will protect you. The snake can't hurt you here. You are safe."

She took them inside and gave them some cookies and milk. She read them a story and sang them a song. They felt comfortable and calm. They forgot about the snake.

The next day, their dad came home from work. He had a surprise for them. He had a big cage with a new pet. It was a rabbit. It was white and fluffy, and it had long ears. It was friendly. It liked to hop and nibble.

"Look, Sam and Mia, I got you a rabbit!" their dad said, smiling.

Their dad laughed and said, "Pebble? That's a funny name. Why do you want to name it Pebble?"

Sam and Mia looked at each other and giggled. They said, "Because it's shiny and pretty, and it's not a snake!"

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with toys. Tom has a big bike. Lily has a small bike. They ride their bikes in the park.

One day, Tom sees a new toy in the shop. It is a fake horse. It has brown fur and a black mane. It can make sounds and move. Tom wants the fake horse. He asks his mom to buy it for him.

"Please, mom, can I have the fake horse? It is so cool. I can ride it like a real horse."

"Sorry, Tom, but the fake horse is too expensive. You already have a bike. You can ride your bike instead."

Tom is sad. He does not want to ride his bike. He wants to ride the fake horse.

The next day, Tom and Lily go to the park. Lily sees the fake horse in the shop window. She thinks it is cute. She asks Tom if he likes it.

"Look, Tom, do you see the fake horse? It is so cute. Do you like it?"

Tom is angry. He does not want to talk about the fake horse. He says to Lily:

"No, I don't like it. It is stupid. It is not a real horse. It is just a toy. It has a stitch on its nose. See? It is broken."

Lily is surprised. She does not see the stitch. She thinks Tom is lying. She says to Tom:

"Tom, why are you lying? I don't see the stitch. The fake horse is not broken. It is fine. You are just jealous. You want the fake horse, but you can't have it."

Tom is ashamed. He knows Lily is right. He is jealous. He wants the fake horse, but he can't have it. He feels bad. He says to Lily:

"Lily, I'm sorry. You are right. I am jealous. I want the fake horse, but I can't have it. I was lying. The fake horse is not stupid. It is cool. I like it."

Lily is happy. She forgives Tom. She says to Tom:

Lily was a bunny who loved to hop. She hopped all day long, from her home to the meadow, from the meadow to the pond, from the pond to the forest. She was happy and free, and did not care about anything else.

One day, she found a pencil on the ground. It was shiny and long, and had a pointy end. Lily was curious and picked it up with her teeth. She thought it was a great toy, and started to hop with it in her mouth.

She met her friend Max, a squirrel, who was looking for nuts. "Hi, Lily!" he said. "What do you have there?"

"It's a pencil!" Lily said proudly. "I found it on the ground. It's great! Look, I can hop with it!"

Max frowned. "Lily, that's not a toy. That's a pencil. People use it to write and draw. You should not hop with it. You could hurt yourself or someone else. You should put it back where you found it, or give it to someone who needs it."

Lily did not listen. She thought Max was silly and jealous. She said, "No, Max. It's mine. I like it. It's fun. Go away!"

She hopped away, leaving Max behind. She did not see the rock in front of her. She tripped and fell, and the pencil poked her in the nose. It hurt a lot, and she started to cry.

Max heard her cry and ran to help her. He took the pencil out of her nose and threw it away. He said, "Lily, are you okay? I'm sorry you got hurt. But I told you, the pencil was not a toy. You should have listened to me. I'm your friend, and I care about you."

Lily felt ashamed and sorry. She said, "Max, you're right. I was wrong. I was selfish and rude. The pencil was not a toy. It was dangerous. I should have listened to you. You're my friend, and you're smart and kind. Thank you for helping me. I'm sorry for being mean to you."

Max smiled and hugged her. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. We all make mistakes. But we can learn from them. Next time, be careful and respectful. And share what you have with others. That's what friends do."

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, Max. You're right. That's what friends do. I'm glad you're my friend. Come on, let's go and play. But not with pencils. With something else. Something safe and fun."

They hopped away, happy and wise. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that pencils are not toys, and that friends are more important than things.

"I'm looking for food. I'm hungry and lost. Do you have any corn or bread for me?" the goose answered.

Tom and Sue felt sorry for the goose. They remembered they had some corn and bread in their lunch boxes. They ran back to their trucks and took out their food. They loaded some corn and bread on one of their trucks and drove it to the fence. They threw the food over the fence to the goose.

"Here you go, goose. This is for you. We hope you like it," Sue said.

The goose was happy and grateful. He ate the corn and bread and felt full and warm. He thanked Tom and Sue for their kindness.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs. Lily found a big worm and showed it to Ben. Ben said, "Wow, that is an interesting worm. Can I touch it?"

Lily said, "Yes, but be gentle. It is very soft and wiggly." She gave the worm to Ben and he held it in his hand. He felt it tickle his palm. He smiled and said, "It is funny. I like it."

Lily said, "Me too. Let's find more worms." They dug some more holes and found more worms. They put them in a bucket and carried them to the house. They wanted to show them to Mom.

Mom was in the kitchen. She was making lunch. She saw Lily and Ben come in with the bucket. She said, "What do you have there, kids?"

Lily and Ben said, "Worms, Mom. We found them in the garden. They are interesting. Look." They opened the bucket and showed Mom the worms.

Mom said, "Oh, my. That is a lot of worms. They are interesting, but they are also dirty. You need to wash your hands before you eat. And you need to put the worms back in the garden. They don't belong in the house."

Lily and Ben said, "OK, Mom. We will wash our hands and put the worms back. But can we keep one worm as a pet?"

Mom said, "No, sweeties. Worms are not good pets. They need to live in the soil and eat leaves. They will not be happy in a cage or a bowl. They will die."

Lily and Ben said, "Oh, no. We don't want the worms to die. We will put them all back. But can we watch them for a little while?"

Mom said, "Yes, you can watch them for a little while. But then you have to put them back. And don't forget to wash your hands."

Lily and Ben said, "Thank you, Mom. You are the best." They hugged Mom and took the bucket to the bathroom. They wanted to watch the worms in the toilet. They thought it would be fun.

They put the bucket on the floor and lifted the lid of the toilet. They were about to pour the worms in when they saw something. It was a big frog. It was sitting on the rim of the toilet. It looked at them and croaked.

Lily and Ben screamed. They dropped the bucket and ran out of the bathroom. They were scared and surprised. They did not expect to see a frog in the toilet.

Mom heard them scream and came to see what was wrong. She saw the frog in the toilet and the worms on the floor. She said, "Oh, dear. How did that frog get in the toilet? And what are all these worms doing here?"

Lily and Ben said, "We don't know, Mom. We found the worms in the garden and we wanted to watch them in the toilet. But then we saw the frog and we got scared. We are sorry, Mom. We made a mess."

Mom said, "It's OK, kids. I'm not mad. But we need to clean up this mess. And we need to get the frog out of the toilet. He doesn't belong there either. He belongs in the pond. Let's get a net and catch him. And let's put the worms back in the garden. They will be happier there."

Lily and Ben said, "OK, Mom. We will help you. We are sorry for the trouble. We learned our lesson. We will not put worms or frogs in the toilet again. It is not fun. It is scary."

Mom said, "That's good, kids. I'm glad you learned your lesson. And I'm proud of you for being brave and helping me. Now let's go and fix this problem. And then we can have lunch. I made your favorite. Sandwiches and juice."

Lily and Ben said, "Yay, Mom. We love you. And we love sandwiches and juice. And we love worms and frogs. But only in the garden and the pond. Not in the toilet."

The end.

They heard a loud boom and saw a flash of light. It was thunder and lightning. They got scared and ran to the bench where their moms were sitting. They hugged their moms and hoped the storm would go away.

Their moms told them not to worry. They said the storm would pass and the sun would come back. They gave them snacks and water and told them stories. They made them laugh and feel better.

Soon, the rain stopped and the cloud moved away. The sun shone again and made the park bright. Lily and Ben smiled and thanked their moms. They grabbed their ball and cones and ran back to the field. They wanted to play soccer again and score a goal. They were happy and not gloomy anymore.

Lily and Sam smile. They are happy. They are compassionate. They did a good thing. They hope the bird will fly again soon. They say goodbye to the bird. They go back to play.

"Let me see the pot!" Tom says. He climbs on a chair and reaches for the pot.

"No, I want to see the pot!" Sam says. He pushes Tom and tries to grab the pot.

The pot is hot and heavy. It falls from the stove and lands on the floor. The pot makes a loud noise. The pot is full of soup. The soup spills everywhere. The soup is hot and wet.

Tom and Sam scream. They are scared and hurt. The soup burns their skin. The pot is rough and hard. The pot hurts their feet.

Mom hears the noise and runs to the kitchen. She sees the mess and the boys. She is angry and sad. She helps the boys and takes them to the bathroom. She puts cold water and cream on their burns. She says:

"Tom and Sam, you are naughty and foolish. You should not play with the pot. The pot is not a toy. The pot is for cooking. You could have been hurt more. You could have broken the pot. You could have started a fire. You should listen to me and stay away from the stove. You should be careful and gentle. You should be sorry and learn your lesson."

The end.

Moral value: Do not play with dangerous things. Listen to your parents. Be careful and gentle.

One day, he saw something shiny in the water. He sailed his boat closer and reached for it. It was a small round thing with a long stick. He did not know what it was, but it looked interesting. He put it in his pocket and took it home.

He showed it to his mom and asked her what it was. She smiled and said it was a microscope. She said it was a tool to see very small things that you cannot see with your eyes. She said it was very special and someone must have lost it.

She took him to the kitchen and gave him a piece of paper and a pencil. She said he could draw what he saw with the microscope. She helped him put the round thing on his eye and the stick on the paper. She said he had to move the stick to make the picture clear.

Ben looked through the microscope and saw amazing things. He saw tiny dots and lines and colors. He saw things that looked like bugs and plants and stars. He was so happy and excited. He drew what he saw on the paper and made a beautiful picture.

He forgot about the gloomy day outside. He forgot about the rain and the clouds and the cold. He only saw the wonderful things in the water and on the paper. Lila was a pretty zebra who liked to run and play with her friends. She wanted to be the fastest zebra in the herd, but she always came last in the races. She felt sad and wished she could succeed.

One day, she met a wise old zebra who saw her trying hard to run faster. He said, "Lila, you have a strong heart and a brave spirit. But you need to learn how to use your stripes to your advantage. They can help you confuse and trick your opponents."

Lila was curious and asked, "How can I do that?"

The old zebra said, "Follow me and I will show you." He led her to a field of tall grass and flowers. He said, "Look at the grass and the flowers. They have many colors and shapes, just like your stripes. When you run, try to blend in with them and change your direction often. That way, you can surprise and outsmart your friends."

Lila nodded and thanked the old zebra. She practiced his advice and soon she felt more confident and clever. She challenged her friends to another race and they agreed. They lined up at the start and waited for the signal.

When the race began, Lila ran like the wind. She used her stripes to hide and switch lanes. She dodged and darted past her friends, who could not keep up with her. She crossed the finish line first and cheered. She had succeeded!

Her friends congratulated her and asked her how she did it. She smiled and said, "I learned a new trick from a wise old zebra. He taught me how to use my stripes to win."

They all wanted to learn the trick too, and Lila was happy to share it. They thanked her and said she was a pretty and smart zebra. Lila felt proud and happy. She had made new friends and learned a new skill. She had a great day.

Lily and Ben wanted to play in the creek. They put on their boots and hats and ran to the water. They saw some sticks and stones and leaves on the ground. They had an idea.

"Let's measure the creek!" Lily said. "We can use the sticks to see how deep it is."

"Good idea!" Ben said. "I will find the longest stick. You find the shortest stick."

They looked around and picked up some sticks. They compared them and saw that Ben had the longest stick and Lily had the shortest stick.

"OK, let's go!" Ben said. He walked to the edge of the creek and put his stick in the water. He pushed it down until it touched the bottom. He looked at the stick and saw how much water was on it.

"The creek is this deep!" he said, showing Lily his stick. "It is not very deep. Maybe we can cross it."

Lily nodded. She walked to the other edge of the creek and put her stick in the water. She pushed it down until it touched the bottom. She looked at the stick and saw how much water was on it.

"The creek is this deep!" she said, showing Ben her stick. "It is very deep. Maybe we cannot cross it."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They looked at their sticks. They looked at the creek. They were confused.

"How can the creek be both deep and not deep?" Ben asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe we measured wrong. Maybe we should try again."

They tried again. They switched sticks. They switched sides. They measured the creek. But they got the same results. The creek was both deep and not deep.

They were frustrated. They wanted to play in the creek, but they did not know how. They did not know what to do.

Then they heard a voice.

"Hello, children. What are you doing?"

They turned around and saw a man. He was wearing a hat and a coat and a bag. He had a smile on his face.

"We are measuring the creek," Ben said.

"We want to play in the creek, but we don't know how deep it is," Lily said.

The man nodded. He walked to the creek and looked at it. He took out something from his bag. It was a long, thin, metal thing. It had numbers on it. It looked like a ruler, but bigger.

"This is a tape measure," the man said. "It can help you measure the creek. Do you want to try it?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They were curious. They wanted to try it.

The man showed them how to use the tape measure. He put one end of it on the ground and the other end in the water. He pulled the tape measure until it was tight. He looked at the numbers on it.

"The creek is 20 centimeters deep here," he said.

He moved to another spot and did the same thing.

"The creek is 40 centimeters deep here," he said.

He moved to another spot and did the same thing.

"The creek is 60 centimeters deep here," he said.

He moved to another spot and did the same thing.

"The creek is 80 centimeters deep here," he said.

He moved to another spot and did the same thing.

"The creek is 100 centimeters deep here," he said.

He moved to the last spot and did the same thing.

"The creek is empty here," he said.

Ben and Lily looked at the spot. They saw that there was no water there. The creek was dry. They were surprised.

"Why is the creek empty here?" Ben asked.

The man shrugged.

"Maybe there is a hole in the ground. Maybe the water goes somewhere else. Maybe the creek is not always the same. Maybe it changes with the rain and the sun and the wind."

He smiled.

"But you see, children, the creek is not both deep and not deep. The creek is different in different places. You have to measure it with something that can show you the difference. Like a tape measure."

He gave them the tape measure.

"Here, you can keep this. You can use it to measure other things. Like trees and rocks and flowers and bugs. You can learn a lot from measuring things. You can have fun with measuring things."

Ben and Lily thanked the man. They took the tape measure. They looked at the creek. They looked at each other. They had a new idea.

"Let's measure the creek!" they said.

They ran to the creek and started to measure it. They measured it in different places. They saw how different it was. They learned a lot from measuring it. They had fun with measuring it.

They played in the creek. They forgot about their sticks. They forgot about their problem. They were happy.
