One day, a polite cat named Max went for a walk in the park. He saw many things that he liked, such as flowers, birds and trees. He also saw some other cats who were playing with a ball of yarn.

"Hello, can I play with you?" Max asked them in a friendly voice.

"Sure, you can join us," one of the cats said. "We are having fun with this yarn. It is soft and colorful."

Max thanked them and went to play with them. He was very good at rolling the yarn, catching it and tossing it. He also shared it with the other cats and waited for his turn.

They played for a long time, until they heard a loud bark. It was a big dog who wanted to chase them. The dog ran towards them, growling and showing his teeth.

"Run, run, run!" the cats shouted. They dropped the yarn and ran away as fast as they could.

Max was scared, but he did not forget to be polite. He picked up the yarn and carried it with him. He ran after the other cats, looking for a safe place to hide.

He saw a fence that was not too high. He used his strong legs to spring over it. He landed on the other side, where there was a nice garden. He saw a little girl who was sitting on a swing.

"Hello, little girl," Max said. "Can I hide here? There is a big dog who wants to catch me."

"Hello, little cat," the girl said. "You can hide here. There is no dog here. You are safe."

"Thank you, little girl," Max said. "You are very kind. Can I give you this yarn? It is a gift for you."

"Thank you, little cat," the girl said. "You are very polite. I like this yarn. It is beautiful. Can I pet you? You are soft and cute."

"Yes, you can pet me," Max said. "I like that. You are gentle and sweet."

They became friends and played together. Max was happy. He had found a new home and a new friend. He was glad that he was polite.

Tom and Mia are playing in their room. They have many toys and clothes. Tom likes to build towers with blocks. Mia likes to dress up with hats and scarves. They are having fun.

But then Tom sees a hanger on the floor. He thinks it is a funny toy. He picks it up and swings it around. He hits Mia's tower with the hanger. The tower falls down and the blocks scatter. Mia is angry.

"Tom, you destroy my tower!" Mia shouts. "That is not a toy, that is a hanger. It is for clothes, not for hitting."

Tom does not listen. He laughs and swings the hanger again. He hits Mia's hat and scarf. They fly off her head and land on the bed. Mia is very angry.

"Tom, you destroy my hat and scarf!" Mia cries. "They are not toys, they are for dressing up. They are mine, not yours."

Tom still does not listen. He thinks it is fun to destroy things. He swings the hanger one more time. He hits a glass on the table. The glass breaks and the juice spills. The juice is sour. It splashes on Tom's face and clothes. Tom is surprised and scared.

"Tom, you destroy the glass and the juice!" Mia says. "They are not toys, they are for drinking. They are sour, not sweet."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Maria. She was three years old and very restless.

Maria stopped twirling. "Mummy, what was that?" She asked her mummy, her eyes widening.

"It was just a bird in the bush honey." Mummy said.

Maria wasn't sure. She held her mummy's hand and slowly walked over to the bush. As she got closer, she heard the voice again.

She peeked around the bush, and there, she saw a fairy! She was tinkling and singing in the sunshine. 

Maria was captivated. She held out her hand and said, "Hello, I'm Maria."

The fairy smiled and replied, "Hello Maria! I'm Enchantra. Would you like to come and play pretend with me?"

Maria giggled and said, "Yes please!" She held Enchantra's hand, and the two went off to find a magical world.

Lily was sad and went home to tell her mom. Her mom reminded her that sometimes people aren't nice and take things that don't belong to them. Lily felt better knowing that her mom loved her and would help her through tough times.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the farm with their mom. They saw many animals, like pigs, chickens, and horses. They also saw a big cow with black and white spots. The boy wanted to touch the cow, but the girl was afraid.

"Come on, it's just a cow," the boy said. "It won't hurt you."

"No, it might bite me or kick me," the girl said. "I don't like cows. They are big and loud and smelly."

The boy thought the girl was ignorant. He thought cows were nice and friendly. He went closer to the cow and reached out his hand. He wanted to pet the cow's nose. But the cow did not like that. The cow moved its head and pinched the boy's finger with its teeth.

"Ow, ow, ow!" the boy cried. "The cow bit me! The cow bit me!"

The girl ran to the boy and hugged him. She felt sorry for him. She also felt a little scared. She did not want the cow to bite her too.

"Are you okay?" the girl asked.

"It hurts, it hurts," the boy said. "The cow is mean. The cow is mean."

Their mom heard them and came to see what happened. She saw the boy's finger was red and swollen. She took him to the car and put some ice on it. She also gave him a hug and a kiss.

"I'm sorry, honey," their mom said. "The cow did not mean to hurt you. The cow was just scared. You should not touch animals without asking first. They might think you are a threat."

The boy nodded. He learned his lesson. He was not ignorant anymore. He also felt a little sorry for the cow. He hoped the cow was not scared anymore. He decided to be more careful and respectful with animals. He also thanked his sister for being nice to him. He realized she was not ignorant either. She was just cautious. He gave her a hug and a kiss too.

Lily was a yellow bird who loved to sing. She sang every morning and every night, and made her friends happy. But one day, a big gray cloud came and covered the sun. Lily felt sad and scared. She did not want to sing anymore.

Her friends noticed that Lily was quiet and asked her what was wrong. Lily said she was afraid of the gray cloud and did not feel like singing. Her friends tried to encourage her. They said the gray cloud would not hurt her, and that her singing was beautiful and bright. They said they missed her voice and wanted to hear it again.

Lily listened to her friends and felt a little better. She decided to try singing again, even if the gray cloud was still there. She opened her beak and sang a soft song. As she sang, she felt more brave and happy. She sang louder and louder, until her song filled the sky.

The gray cloud heard Lily's song and was surprised. It had never heard such a lovely sound before. It felt curious and moved closer to see who was singing. As it did, it saw Lily and her friends, who were all yellow and cheerful. The gray cloud felt a warm feeling in its heart. It wanted to be friends with them, too.

The gray cloud smiled and said hello to Lily and her friends. It said it was sorry for scaring them, and that it liked Lily's song. It said it wanted to share the sun with them, and moved aside to let the light shine through. Lily and her friends were happy and thanked the gray cloud. They invited it to join them and sing along. The gray cloud agreed and learned some of their songs. They all sang together and had fun.

The moral of the story is: Don't be afraid of things that are different from you. You can make new friends and learn new things if you are kind and brave. And always remember to sing your song, even when the sky is gray.

"Can I have some salt, please?" Tom asked. He liked his soup salty.

Tom took the jar and shook it over his soup. He shook it too hard. The lid came off and all the salt fell into his bowl.

"Oh no!" Tom cried. "My soup is too salty now!"

Sue laughed. She thought it was funny. She picked up her spoon and tasted her soup. It was just right.

"Can I have some of your soup, please?" Tom asked Sue. He was hungry and his soup was ruined.

"No, you can't," Sue said. She was fierce. She did not want to share her soup. "You should be careful with the salt. It is your fault."

Tom was sad. He did not like Sue's answer. He looked at Mom. He hoped she would help him.

Mom saw what happened. She was kind. She got up and went to the kitchen. She came back with another bowl of soup for Tom.

"Here you go, Tom," Mom said. She gave him the new bowl of soup. "This soup is not too salty. You can enjoy it."

"Thank you, Mom," Tom said. He smiled. He was happy. He took a sip of his soup. It was delicious.

Sue saw that Mom was nice to Tom. She felt sorry for being fierce. She decided to be nice too.

"Tom, do you want some of my bread?" Sue asked. She offered him a piece of her bread.

"Sure, thank you, Sue," Tom said. He took the bread and ate it. It was soft and warm.

Tom and Sue shared their lunch. They were not fierce anymore. They were friendly. Mom was proud of them. She hugged them and kissed them. They had a good lunch.

Tom says, "No, you can't. It is my pen. Go away."

Sam feels sad and hurt. He says, "But we are friends. Friends share things. Why are you so mean?"

Tom says, "I don't care. This is my pen and I don't want to share it. Leave me alone."

Sam walks away and finds another friend, Lily. Lily is friendly and kind. She has a pen too, but she is happy to share it with Sam. They draw together and have fun.

Tom sees Sam and Lily playing and feels lonely. He realizes that his new pen is not worth losing his friend. He decides to be nice and share his pen with Sam. He walks over to Sam and Lily and says, "I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong. You can try my new pen. It is not only mine, it is ours. Can we be friends again?"

Sam smiles and says, "Of course, Tom. I'm glad you changed your mind. Thank you for sharing your pen. Come and play with us."

Tom joins Sam and Lily and they draw together and have fun. They all share their pens and paper and have more colors and ideas. They learn that sharing is caring and that being friendly is better than being selfish.

Lily and Tom are bored. They have nothing to do. They look at the television, but it is dull. The same shows are on every day. They want to go outside and play, but it is raining.

"Can we go to the park, Mom?" Lily asks.

"No, dear, it is too wet. You will catch a cold," Mom says.

"Can we go to the library, Mom?" Tom asks.

"No, dear, it is too far. You will get muddy," Mom says.

Lily and Tom sigh. They sit on the couch and watch the television. They wish they could go somewhere fun.

Then, they hear a knock on the door. They run to see who it is. It is their friend Sam. He has a big smile on his face.

"Hi, Lily and Tom! Do you want to go to the circus with me?" Sam asks.

"The circus?" Lily and Tom say.

"Yes, the circus! There are clowns, and animals, and tricks, and popcorn! It is not dull at all! My dad has tickets for us. Come on, let's go!" Sam says.

Lily and Tom look at Mom. Mom nods and smiles.

"Okay, you can go to the circus. But wear your coats and boots. And have fun!" Mom says.

Lily and Tom grab their coats and boots. They hug Mom and thank her. They follow Sam to his car. They are not bored anymore. They are excited. They are going to the circus!

One day, they decided to play a game of hide and seek. Anna said, "I will count to ten and you hide. Then I will find you." Ben nodded and ran to the wardrobe. He opened the door and crawled inside. He saw some coats and shoes and a big box. He thought it was a good hiding place.

Anna counted to ten and then shouted, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looked under the bed, behind the curtains, and in the closet. She could not find Ben. She wondered where he was. They had fun playing with the stuffed animals in the wardrobe. They forgot about the time and the game. They did not hear Mom calling them for lunch. They only heard the roar of the lion, the growl of the bear, and the laughter of each other.

Lily and Max were twins who liked to play in the park. They loved to slide, swing, and run around with their friends. But sometimes they got bored of the same games and wanted to try something new.

One day, they saw a big sign that said "Wild Animal Show". It had pictures of lions, tigers, monkeys, and other animals that they had never seen before. They asked their mom if they could go and watch the show. Their mom said yes, but they had to follow some rules.

"Listen to me, Lily and Max," their mom said. "The animals in the show are wild, not like our dog Spot. They can be dangerous if you get too close or make too much noise. You have to stay with me and do what I say. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded and said yes. They were very excited to see the wild animals. They followed their mom to the show and found some seats. The show was about to start.

The first animal that came out was a lion. He was big and yellow and had a long mane. He roared loudly and made everyone jump. The trainer told the lion to do some tricks, like jumping through a hoop and sitting on a stool. He used a whip and a chair to order the lion what to do.

Lily and Max watched with wide eyes. They thought the lion was amazing, but also scary. They wanted to see more animals, but they also wanted to be safe. They held their mom's hand and did not make a sound.

The next animal that came out was a monkey. He was small and brown and had a long tail. He was very funny and made everyone laugh. He did some tricks, like riding a bike and wearing a hat. He did not need a whip or a chair to order him what to do. He listened to the trainer and got some bananas as a reward.

Lily and Max watched with delight. They thought the monkey was cute, but also smart. They wanted to play with the monkey, but they also knew he was wild. They stayed in their seats and clapped their hands.

The last animal that came out was a tiger. He was big and orange and had black stripes. He was very fast and strong. He did some tricks, like jumping over a fire and balancing on a ball. He used his teeth and claws to show who was the boss. He did not listen to the trainer or anyone else. He did what he wanted to do.

Lily and Max watched with fear. They thought the tiger was beautiful, but also dangerous. They did not want to see the tiger, but they also could not look away. They hid behind their mom and hoped the show would end soon.

But then something happened. The tiger saw Lily and Max and their mom. He did not like them. He wanted to scare them or hurt them. He growled and ran towards them. He broke the fence and jumped into the crowd. Everyone screamed and ran away.

Lily and Max were very scared. They did not know what to do. They wanted their mom to protect them, but she was also scared. She did not know what to do either.

But then someone else came. It was Spot, their dog. He had followed them to the park and to the show. He saw the tiger and his family. He did not like the tiger. He wanted to save his family. He barked and ran towards the tiger. He bit the tiger's tail and made him angry.

The tiger turned around and saw Spot. He did not like Spot. He wanted to fight Spot. He roared and ran towards Spot. He tried to bite Spot's neck and make him stop.

But Spot was brave and smart. He dodged the tiger's teeth and claws. He ran around the tiger and made him dizzy. He barked louder and louder and made him confused.

The trainer saw what was happening. He grabbed his whip and his chair and ran towards the tiger and Spot. He ordered the tiger to stop and go back to his cage. He helped Spot and praised him for his courage.

Lily and Max saw what was happening. They were very happy and proud. They ran towards Spot and hugged him and thanked him for his help. They said he was the best dog ever.

Their mom saw what was happening. She was very relieved and grateful. She ran towards Spot and her children and hugged them and kissed them. She said they were the perfect family.

The end.

Timmy heard another voice on the phone. It was Anna. She said, "Let him go, or I'll call the police. I saw you from the window. I have your picture. I have your license plate. You have no choice. Surrender."

The man dropped the phone. He looked at Timmy. He looked at the window. He looked at the door. He was trapped. He was scared. He let go of Timmy and said, "OK, OK, you win. I surrender. Don't call the police. Please."

Timmy ran to the door. He opened it and saw Anna. She hugged him and said, "You're safe, Timmy. You're brave. I'm sorry I couldn't find you sooner. I love you."

Timmy hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Anna. You're smart. You're strong. You saved me."

One day, Ben and Lily decided to spend the afternoon in the garden. They took their shovels and buckets and made a big castle in the sandbox. They put some shells and stones on the castle to make it look pretty. Then they took turns on the swing and the slide. They had a lot of fun.

"Look, Lily, the rose bush has a new flower!" Ben said, pointing to a big red rose that had bloomed. "It's so pretty! Can we pick it and give it to mom?"

Lily nodded. She loved her mom and wanted to make her happy. They walked over to the rose bush and reached for the flower. But as they touched the stem, they felt something sharp and prickly.

"Ow!" Ben and Lily cried, pulling back their hands. They saw some drops of blood on their fingers. They had been stung by the thorns.

The rose bush was tough. It did not want to give away its flower. It wanted to keep it for itself.

Ben and Lily ran to their mom, who was sitting on the porch. They showed her their fingers and told her what happened.

"Oh, you poor things!" mom said, hugging them. She took them inside and washed their fingers. She put some cream and a band-aid on each wound. She kissed them and said, "You are very brave and sweet to want to give me a rose. But you don't have to. I love you just the way you are."

Ben and Lily smiled. They felt better. They hugged their mom and said, "We love you too, mom. You are the best."

They went back to the garden and played some more. They did not touch the rose bush again. They knew it was tough. But they also knew it was beautiful. And they were happy to share the garden with it.

But the duck is not really grateful. The duck is greedy. The duck wants all the pebbles. The duck does not like to share. The duck has a plan.

The duck pretends to be friendly. The duck says, "Children, you are so nice. Can you come closer to me? I want to give you a hug."

Tim and Sue trust the duck. They walk to the edge of the water. They want to hug the duck.

But the duck is not nice. The duck is mean. The duck grabs Tim and Sue with its beak and pulls them into the water. The duck wants to eat them.

Tim and Sue scream. They are scared. They try to get away. But the duck is strong. The duck is hungry. The duck does not care.

The duck eats Tim and Sue. The duck is full. The duck is happy. The duck has all the pebbles.

One day, his son Tom came to visit him at his office. Tom was three years old and liked to have fun. He saw a big chair with wheels in front of Tim's desk. He climbed on it and started to spin. He laughed and shouted, "Whee! This is fun!"

Tom stopped spinning and looked at his father. He said, "But Daddy, why are you always working? Don't you want to play with me? Don't you want to be happy?"

Tim felt a pang in his heart. He realized that he had been neglecting his son and his own joy. He said, "You are right, Tom. I have been working too much and forgetting to have fun. I'm sorry. Come here, let me hug you."

He got up from his desk and hugged his son. He said, "I love you, Tom. You are more important than any papers or books. Let's go home and play together. And maybe we can spin on the chair a little bit."

Tom smiled and hugged his father back. He said, "I love you too, Daddy. You are the best lawyer and the best father. Thank you for playing with me."

They left the office and went home. Tim felt happier and lighter than he had in a long time. He learned that he should not let his work take over his life. He learned that he should spend more time with his son and enjoy the simple things. He learned that spinning on a chair can be fun.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a wet frog named Fred. Fred loved to jump in the puddles after it rained. One sunny day, after a big rain, Fred met a new friend named Harry. Harry was a big animal with a long horn on his head.

"Hi, I'm Fred," said the wet frog. "Do you like to play in the puddles too?"

"No, I don't like to get wet," said Harry, shaking his big horn. "I like to stay dry in the sun."

Fred thought for a moment and then smiled. "I have an idea! Let's play a game. You can stay dry in the sun, and I will jump in the puddles. When I am wet, I will try to make you wet too by shaking the water off me."

Harry laughed and agreed to play the game. They played all day long. Fred would jump in the puddles and try to make Harry wet, but Harry would use his big horn to block the water. They laughed and had so much fun together.

At the end of the day, Fred and Harry were both tired but happy. They had made a new friend and found a fun game to play together. From that day on, they played together in the forest, with Fred always trying to make Harry wet and Harry always trying to stay dry.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom was an adventurous boy who loved to play outside. One day, he saw a big apple tree in his yard. The tree had many red apples on it. Tom wanted to eat the apples, but they were too high for him to reach.

Tom had an idea. He called his friend, Sam, and said, "Let's joke and play by the apple tree. Maybe we can find a way to get the apples." Sam agreed and they both went to the tree. They tried to climb, but it was too hard. They tried to jump, but they couldn't reach. Then, Tom saw a long stick on the ground.

Tom picked up the stick and said, "I will use this stick to get the apples." Sam laughed, thinking it was a joke. But Tom was serious. He swung the stick at the apples, trying to knock them down. One apple fell, but it was not enough. Tom swung the stick harder and harder, trying to get more apples.

Suddenly, the stick hit a big branch and the branch broke. The broken branch fell down and landed on Tom's foot. Tom cried out in pain, and Sam ran to get help. Tom's mom came and saw what happened. She was very sad and worried. Tom had to go to the doctor, and he could not play outside for a long time.

From that day on, Tom learned not to be too adventurous. He never tried to get apples with a stick again. And every time he saw an apple tree, he remembered the day he got hurt and decided not to take risks he was not ready for.

Lily was a little girl who liked to clap her hands. She clapped when she was happy, when she saw something funny, or when she wanted to make noise. She clapped so much that her parents and her brother sometimes got annoyed.

One night, Lily had a bad dream. She dreamed that she was in a dark and gloomy place, where there were no colors, no toys, and no friends. She felt scared and lonely, and she wanted to clap her hands to make some sound. But when she tried to clap, she found that her hands were stuck together. She could not move them, or make any noise. She felt even more scared and lonely, and she started to cry.

She woke up with a loud scream, and her parents and her brother rushed to her room. They saw her crying and shaking, and they asked her what was wrong. Lily told them about her nightmare, and how she could not clap her hands. Her parents hugged her and told her that it was only a dream, and that she could clap her hands as much as she wanted. Her brother gave her a toy and told her a joke to make her laugh.

Lily felt better, and she thanked her parents and her brother. She clapped her hands to show them how happy she was. But then, something strange happened. Every time she clapped, a loud thunder boomed in the sky. The room became dark and gloomy, and the wind howled outside. Lily, her parents, and her brother looked out the window, and they saw that a big storm was coming. They were all very afraid, and they wondered what was going on.

Lily realized that her nightmare had come true. She had clapped so much that she had made the weather angry. She felt very sorry, and she wished she had not clapped so much. She learned that clapping was not always good, and that sometimes it was better to be quiet and listen.

The end.

Moral: Clapping is fun, but too much of it can cause trouble. Be careful what you wish for, and respect the feelings of others.

"Look, Lily, I have a white rose for you!" Sara said, holding the flower in front of the doll's face. "Do you like it?"

"Yes, I like it, thank you, Sara!" Lily said, in Sara's voice.

Sara smiled and hugged Lily. She liked to repeat what Lily would say, if she could talk. She thought it was fun.

She put the white rose in Lily's hair and said, "Now you look like a princess, Lily! Do you want to play tea party with me?"

"Yes, I want to play tea party with you, Sara!" Lily said, in Sara's voice.

Sara clapped and ran to get her tea set. She poured some water in the cups and pretended it was tea. She gave one cup to Lily and one to herself.

"Cheers, Lily!" Sara said, tapping her cup against Lily's.

"Cheers, Sara!" Lily said, in Sara's voice.

Sara giggled and drank her water. She was very happy to have Lily as her friend. She loved her doll and her white rose.

"No, Mom said we have to remain outside until lunch," said Kim.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the forest. They liked to collect things they found, like leaves, stones, and feathers. One day, they saw a big log near a stream. It was brown and smooth, and had many holes.

"Look, Ben, a log!" Lily said. "Maybe we can find some bugs or animals inside."

"Let's go and see," Ben said. They ran to the log and looked at the holes. They saw some ants, a spider, and a snail.

"Wow, so many friends!" Lily said. She wanted to touch them, but Ben stopped her.

"Be careful, Lily. Some bugs can bite or sting. And we should not bother them. They live here, and this is their home."

Lily nodded. She understood. She did not want to hurt the bugs or make them sad. She looked around and saw some flowers and berries.

"Hey, Ben, I have an idea. Why don't we collect some flowers and berries, and give them to the bugs as a gift? Maybe they will like them, and we can be friends."

Ben smiled. He liked Lily's idea. He thought she was very generous and kind. He agreed to collect some flowers and berries with her. They picked some yellow, red, and purple ones, and some juicy, sweet ones. They put them in a basket they had brought.

They went back to the log and placed the basket near the holes. They hoped the bugs would see it and enjoy it.

"Hello, bugs," Lily said softly. "We brought you some flowers and berries. We hope you like them. We want to be your friends. We are Ben and Lily. Thank you for letting us see your home."

They waited for a while, but they did not see any bugs come out. They wondered if the bugs were shy or scared.

"Maybe they are sleeping, or busy," Ben said. "Or maybe they need some time to trust us. We can come back another day, and see if they are here."

Lily nodded. She hoped the bugs would like their gift, and be happy. She wanted to see them again.

"OK, Ben. Let's go home now. We can come back tomorrow, and bring some more flowers and berries. Maybe then we can talk to the bugs, and play with them."

They held hands and walked back to their house. They were happy and proud of their collection. They had found a new place to explore, and maybe some new friends to make.

She was so excited that she started exploring the garden. Suddenly, Janie heard a voice. It was coming from a small bush. She stepped closer and saw two little animals looking at her. It was a fox and a rabbit.

The fox said to the rabbit, "We have to choose. Do we trust Janie or do we run away?"
The rabbit answered, "I don't know, I feel so guilty. What should I do?"

Janie smiled and said, "you don't have to be afraid, I won't hurt you. I'm a friend. You can trust me."
The little animals looked at each other, smiled back and choose to trust Janie. 

Janie and the animal became best of friends and they all lived happily ever after.

One day, Daisy noticed something different about Spot. Spot had started to shrink! Spot was getting smaller and smaller each day. Daisy was very confused and asked Spot what was happening to him. 

Spot told Daisy that whenever he ate the grass off the ranch he would shrink a little bit. Daisy became very jealous because she wanted to be able to shrink too. 

Spot and Daisy decided to ask the ranch-owner for some advice. The ranch-owner told them that they could take special vitamins to help them grow. 

So Spot and Daisy started taking the vitamins and they soon stopped shrinking. Spot and Daisy were happy once again and they enjoyed the rest of their summer on the ranch.

The girl encouraged the gem and told it, "You can do it!" The gem felt better and strong. It knew it could do it.

The girl smiled and said, "Let's do this together!" She put the small gem on her hand and the gem felt safe.

They went on a special journey together and the gem had so much fun. The gem was so happy and thanked the girl for being so kind. They hugged and said goodbye, but the gem never forgot the girl's encouragement.

One day, there was a duck who was walking around in a pond. The duck was very obedient and always listened to all the directions the farmer gave him. He was the best duck that the farmer had ever had!

One day, the farmer wanted the duck to collect some food for his dinner. The duck was happy to do it, but he had to hurry or he would delay the farmer's dinner.

He hopped on the pond and began swimming. However, the pond was a lot larger than he had thought and he was swimming very slowly. He tried as hard as he could but he couldn't catch all the food that he needed in time.

The farmer saw what was happening and said, "Oh dear, why are you being so slow, duck? You must hurry up or else you'll delay my dinner!"

The duck listened to the farmer and tried harder than ever to go as fast as he could. Eventually, he was able to gather all the food in time and the farmer enjoyed his dinner without a delay. The duck was so happy that he had been obedient and done his job.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old. One day, Daisy wanted to cook something special.

She went to the kitchen, opened a cupboard, and found some eggs. She cracked the eggs into a bowl and added some milk. She stirred the mixture with a spoon.

Suddenly, Daisy heard a loud noise behind her. She got frightened and put her thumb in her mouth. When she turned around, Daisy saw a big, furry mouse standing beside her.

"What are you cooking?" asked the mouse.

"Pancakes," Daisy replied softly.

"I love pancakes!" said the mouse. "Can I try one?"

Daisy smiled and nodded. She cooked the pancakes on the stove. When they were ready, Daisy and the mouse enjoyed their pancakes together. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny called Ben. Ben was a very curious bunny who liked to explore and try new things. One day, Ben decided to explore a mysterious cave. As he was hopping inside, he noticed something strange: a magnet! He picked it up, but soon after he picked it up, the magnet vanished! 

He couldn't believe it until he heard a voice behind him. It was a wizard! The wizard said, "I can make your magnet reappear if you do one thing for me." Ben was a brave bunny, so he said, "Yes, I'll do it!"

The wizard asked Ben to make a serious promise that he would never bother him or the cave again. Ben promised! 

The wizard said, "Great! As promised, here is your magnet!" Suddenly, the magnet reappeared right in Ben's hand!

Ben was so happy and thanked the wizard. He promised to keep his promise and never come back to bother the wizard or the cave again! Ben went back home, with the magnet in his hand, never to forget the wonderful mysterious cave.

The kids who were visiting were very sad. They couldn't believe their eyes.

Then, a fairy appeared in the sky and said: "Don't worry! I'll bring the animals back." 

The fairy waved her wand and suddenly the zoo was full of animals again. 

The kids jumped with joy and ran around the zoo to see their favourite animals. 

The fairy said: "I'm glad to see you happy. Enjoy the original zoo!" 

And with a twinkle of her wand, the fairy disappeared.

Jack was having a miserable day. Everywhere he went, people seemed to ignore him. He felt so small and helpless as he trudged along.

As he continued walking, a mule came up to him and blocked his way. Jack was surprised, but the mule seemed different than the people who had been ignoring him. The mule looked at Jack kindly, as if it was trying to say something.

Inspired by the mule's friendly gaze, Jack hugged it tight. The mule accepted the hug, and the two began walking together. Soon, Jack felt his mood rising. He had a new companion, and he was no longer alone.

But then, all of a sudden, the mule took a detour, and Jack had to go on his own again. He was sad for a moment, but then he realized that the mule had not been ignoring him, but instead leaving him to teach him an important lesson: He should never give up, and always keep going no matter how miserable the journey may be.

Once upon a time, there was a frog who lived in a pond. One day he decided to jump out of the pond and practice his jumping skills. He jumped from one rock to another, from one lily pad to another, and got really excited. His jumping got more and more impressive with each leap.

One day, the frog ran into a turtle on the edge of the pond. The frog was excited to meet someone new and asked the turtle why he wasn't in the pond.

"I'm not in the pond because I'm trying to improve my crawling", the turtle said.

The frog was puzzled and asked the turtle, "Don't you crawl better in the water?"

The turtle smiled and said, "No, because I need practice! When I practice, I get better and better. Improvement comes from practice, not just from being in the pond."

The frog smiled in understanding. He said goodbye to the turtle and jumped back into the pond. From then on, he practiced his jumping every day until eventually he was able to make impressive leaps.

The moral of the story is that with practice and dedication you can improve no matter where you are.

He looked for the waffle mix, but he could not find it. He saw a bag of flour, a carton of eggs, and a bottle of milk. He thought, maybe I can make my own waffle mix. He poured some flour, some eggs, and some milk into a big bowl. He stirred it with a spoon. It looked lumpy and runny. He did not know what else to do.

He opened the waffle maker and poured some of the mix on one plate. He closed the other plate on top and pressed the handle. He waited for a few minutes. He smelled something burning. He opened the waffle maker and saw a black and sticky mess. He tried to pull it out, but it was stuck. He started to cry.

Mom and dad heard Timmy crying and came to the kitchen. They saw the waffle maker and the bowl of mix. They saw Timmy's sad face. They hugged him and said, "What happened, Timmy?"

Timmy said, "I wanted to make waffles for you, but I did not have waffle mix. I tried to make my own, but it did not work. I failed."

Mom and dad smiled and said, "Timmy, you did not fail. You tried something new and creative. That is very brave and smart. You are a flexible thinker. Sometimes things do not work out the way we want, but we can learn from our mistakes and try again. You can succeed if you keep trying."

They helped Timmy clean up the waffle maker and the bowl. They showed him where the waffle mix was and how to measure and mix it. They let him pour the mix on the waffle maker and press the handle. They watched the light turn green and opened the waffle maker. They saw a golden and crispy waffle. They cheered and clapped.

Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Timmy. And we love your waffle. It is delicious." They ate the waffle together and shared a hug. Timmy felt proud and happy. He succeeded.

The old man smiled and said, "I am a historian. I study the past and the people who lived before us. I have been looking for this tablet for a long time. It was lost in a war many years ago. I am very happy that you found it. Can I see it, please?"

When he woke up, the sun was setting and it was time to go back to his burrow. Benny was so happy that he found the carrots and had a good nap. From that day on, Benny knew where to find the carrots and he never had to be frustrated again.

One day, Lily's mommy gave her a big chocolate bar. Lily was so happy and excited to eat it. But she forgot to put it away and left it outside in the sun. When she came back, the chocolate had melted and spoiled. Lily was sad that she couldn't eat it anymore.

But then, she saw a butterfly fluttering by. Lily chased after it, running through the grass. She forgot all about the spoiled chocolate and had fun playing outside instead.

Once upon a time, there was a big pig. The pig lived on a farm with other animals. One day, the pig saw a bell and wanted to ring it. But the bell was too high for the pig to reach. 

The pig asked for help from the other animals on the farm. The cow tried to reach the bell with her long neck, but she couldn't. The chicken tried to fly up to the bell, but she couldn't. 

Then the dog had an idea. He ran to the farmer's house and barked until the farmer came out. The dog led the farmer to the bell and barked again. The farmer understood and opened the gate to let the pig out. The pig ran to the bell and rang it with his nose. 

Everyone on the farm was happy and cheered for the pig. From that day on, the pig became known as the bell-ringing pig.

The bear didn't listen and jumped into the river. Suddenly, the water was too strong and the bear couldn't swim. He was scared and called for help. His friends heard him and quickly ran to hug him. They pulled him out of the river and the bear realized he should have listened to his friends. 

From that day on, the bear always listened to his friends and never went into the river alone again. He was happy to have such caring friends who warned him when something was not safe.

He found a new wheel and put it on the car. Mia was so happy to see her car fixed. She played with her car all day and thanked Grandpa for fixing it.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a yellow buckle. She wanted to put it on her shoe. Her friend, Tom, saw the buckle too. He said, "No, Mia! The buckle is mine!" Mia said, "No, it is mine!" They both wanted the yellow buckle.

Tom and Mia did not know what to do. Mia said, "Let's ask Mom!" They went to Mia's mom. Mia's mom said, "You both can use the yellow buckle. You can take turns." Mia and Tom did not like this idea. They both wanted the buckle now.

Mia and Tom went back to the yellow buckle. Mia said, "I will use it first!" Tom said, "No, I will!" They both tried to pull the buckle. Mia's mom came and saw them. She said, "You both need to share." Mia and Tom looked at each other. They knew they had to share. Mia let Tom use the buckle first. After Tom, Mia used the buckle. They both were happy. They learned to share and had fun with the yellow buckle.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a chubby cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to cook. Every day, she would cook yummy food for all her friends.

One sunny day, Kitty invited her best friend, a little dog named Buddy, to her house. "Come over, Buddy," said Kitty. "I will cook something nice for us to eat." Buddy was very happy and wagged his tail.

When Buddy arrived at Kitty's house, they both went to the kitchen. Kitty cooked a big pot of soup with lots of tasty things inside. They sat down and ate the soup together. It was so good that they ate it all up. After they finished eating, they played and laughed. Kitty and Buddy had a great day together in the small town.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a kind monkey named Momo. Momo liked to create things. He made toys from leaves and sticks for his friends. All the animals in the jungle loved Momo.

One day, Momo met a sad little bird named Bibi. Bibi had lost her nest in a big storm. Momo wanted to help her. He said, "Don't be sad, Bibi. I will create a new nest for you."

Momo worked very hard. He found many sticks and leaves. He put them together to make a new nest for Bibi. The nest was warm and cozy. Bibi was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Momo. You are a kind friend."

From that day on, Momo and Bibi were the best of friends. They played together in the jungle every day. All the animals knew that Momo was a kind monkey who loved to create things for his friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy plastic cups. Lily thought her cups were very important. She would play with them every day.

One sunny day, Lily decided to measure water with her plastic cups. She filled one cup with water and poured it into another cup. She did this again and again, having lots of fun.

Her mom saw her and smiled. She knew that Lily was learning something important while playing. Lily played with her plastic cups all day, measuring water and feeling very happy.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a powerful flower. This flower was very pretty and strong. All the other flowers looked up to it. They wanted to be just like the powerful flower.

One day, a naughty boy came to the garden. He saw the powerful flower and wanted to destroy it. The boy pulled and pulled at the flower, but it would not come out of the ground.

The powerful flower was very strong and did not let the boy destroy it. The other flowers were very happy and proud of the powerful flower. They knew that they were safe in the garden with the powerful flower to protect them. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim found an interesting magnet. It was red and shiny. He liked to play with it a lot. He could stick it to the fridge and it would hold his drawings. Tim thought the magnet was magic.

Tim had a friend named Sally. He wanted to show her the magnet. "Look, Sally!" Tim said. "This magnet is so cool!" Sally looked at the magnet and smiled. "Wow, it is very interesting," she said. They played with the magnet together, sticking it to different things.

Then, Tim had an idea. "Let's play hide and seek with the magnet!" he said. Sally agreed. They took turns hiding the magnet and finding it. They had so much fun playing with the interesting magnet all day long.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a great wish. She wanted to supply food to all the animals in the forest.

One sunny day, Mia took a big basket and filled it with fruits and vegetables. She walked into the forest with a big smile. She met a bunny, a squirrel, and a bird. Mia gave them some of the food from her basket. They were very happy.

Mia felt great because her wish came true. She went back home with an empty basket and a full heart. From that day on, Mia would always supply food to her animal friends in the forest. They loved her and she loved them too.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a ball that he liked to throw. One day, he saw his friend, Sam. Sam was a reliable friend. They liked to play together.

Tim asked Sam, "Do you want to play with my ball?" Sam said, "Yes, I want to play with your ball!" They started to throw the ball to each other. They were having fun.

But then, Tim had an opinion. He said, "Let's throw the ball very high!" Sam said, "I don't know. That might not be good." But Tim did not listen. He threw the ball very high. The ball went up, up, up, and then it got stuck in a tree. They could not get the ball back. Tim and Sam were sad.

The moral of the story is to listen to your reliable friends because they can help you make good choices.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was enthusiastic about everything. He loved to play, run, and jump all day long.

One day, Tim had to wake up very early. He did not like it. Tim said, "I hate waking up early!" But his mom told him it was a special day. They were going to the park to play with his friends.

At the park, Tim forgot about hating the wake. He played with his friends and had so much fun. They ran, jumped, and laughed all day. In the end, Tim was happy he woke up early for such a great day.
